# **17. Risk Management** 

Risk Management continued to remain an integral part of the Company’s governance framework during FY 2025–26, enabling monitoring of key business risks, proactive identification, assessment and mitigation. 

To align Company’s Risk Management best practices with leading national and international Oil & Gas companies and with ISO 31000:2018 (Risk Management - Guidelines), a comprehensive reassessment of the Company’s Risk Management Policy, Risk Register and procedure was undertaken. 

Based on the findings of the reassessment, Company’s Board in its 572<sup>nd</sup> Meeting held on 09.10.2025 approved the revised Risk Management Policy, 2025 and Updated Risk Register ensuring organizational resilience, informed decision-making, regulatory compliance, and sustainable performance. 

As part of the review exercise, the Company’s risk universe was rationalized and streamlined, resulting in a reduction in the number of identified risks. 

As of March 2026, Enterprise-level risks were determined and monitored under the Company’s Risk Management Framework. These risks were categorized into three broad segments to facilitate focused risk oversight and effective mitigation planning. The portfolio comprised Strategic Risks, which are associated with the achievement of long-term organizational objectives, business sustainability, growth opportunities and external market dynamics. Core Function Risks were identified across key operational and business processes that directly impact the Company’s value chain, operational efficiency, production, and service delivery. The Support Function Risks pertain to enabling functions such as finance, human resources, information technology, legal, procurement, administration and other support services that are essential for sustaining business operations. 

The Company strengthened its risk governance practices through the timely conduct of Risk Management Committee (RMC), Risk Management Steering Committee (RMSC) & Operational Risk Management Committee (ORMC) meetings across all operational spheres and corporate functions. These meetings served as key platforms for periodic review of identified risks, assessment of mitigation measures and evaluation of emerging risk scenarios impacting business operations. 

117 



The Company has adopted a structured Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework aligned with its strategic objectives and operational priorities. Regular risk assessments are carried out across all business functions to identify emerging risks and evaluate their potential impact on operations, financial performance, and long-term sustainability. Continuous monitoring mechanisms were strengthened through enhanced reporting systems and improved risk analytics. Special emphasis was placed on risks related to operational safety, project execution, digital transformation, regulatory compliance, cyber security, supply chain disruptions and environmental sustainability. 

Risk ownership was clearly defined across business units to ensure accountability and timely response. Capacitybuilding initiatives and awareness programs are undertaken to further strengthen the risk management culture across the organization. As part of these efforts, reputed consultants were engaged to conduct Risk Management workshops aimed at enhancing awareness, knowledge, and capabilities among risk stakeholders. Through these measures, the Company remains committed to safeguarding stakeholder value and ensuring sustainable growth in an evolving business environment. 

# **18. Start-Up Initiatives** 

Startup India is a flagship initiative launched by the Government of India on 16<sup>th</sup> January, 2016 aimed at fostering a vibrant startup ecosystem by promoting innovation and entrepreneurship. The programme seeks to drive sustainable economic growth while creating significant employment opportunities across the country. In line with this national vision, the Company has introduced the  Start-up Nurturing, Enabling, and Handholding (SNEH) programme to support and accelerate innovative entrepreneurial ventures. 

Under SNEH, the Company has entered into Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) with five leading institutions—IIT Guwahati, Guwahati Biotech Park, IIT Bhubaneswar, IIM Lucknow, and IIT Delhi—for incubation support. The Company has completed 11 rounds of startup screening and evaluation, disbursing grants of 17.92 crore to startups and 6.19 crore to incubation centres. So far, the Company has supported 25 startups through the grant mechanism. Additionally, 15 startups are in the final stage of selection for investment through Company’s upcoming Alternate Investment Fund (AIF). 

The Company is in the process of setting up ‘OIL SNEH Venture Scheme’ as a Category I Alternate Investment Fund (AIF). The Fund has been conceptualized in the context of India’s ongoing structural economic transformation, driven by rapid industrialization, the energy transition, expansion of the manufacturing sector, digital innovation, and strong policy support for technology-led growth. It aims to establish itself as a strategically differentiated Category I Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) by leveraging the Sponsor, Company’s deep sectoral expertise and institutional credibility, while drawing on the Investment Manager’s capabilities in innovation, incubation, and venture building to support high-potential startups and emerging enterprises. The Fund represents not merely a financial investment vehicle, but also a platform intended to facilitate technology adoption, innovation engagement, and ecosystem development aligned with the Startup India Mission. 

More recently, the Company has joined hands with other Oil & Gas Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) to consolidate and strengthen the startup incubation and investment ecosystem across India’s energy sector. As part of this collaborative initiative, the ‘MC2 Foundation’ has been established as a dedicated institutional platform to promote innovation and sustainable entrepreneurship. The Foundation aims to foster, incubate, mentor, accelerate, and support startups aligned with India’s energy transition and national development priorities. It is currently spearheading the establishment of the ‘MC2 Alternative Investment Fund (AIF)’ to catalyse investments in high-potential startups and emerging technologies across the energy value chain. 

The Company supported Startups under its initiative SNEH have made significant strides in driving innovation and technological advancement in various sectors. These startups have contributed to areas such as clean energy solutions, Green Hydrogen, Clean Mobility, Oilfield Solutions, Carbon Capturing, Environmental Sustainability, Healthcare, Artificial Intelligence, Robotics etc. Several of them have successfully developed indigenous technologies that reduce operational costs and environmental impact. By fostering innovation through funding, mentorship and strategic collaboration, Company’s startup initiatives contributing immensely to the startup ecosystem of our country. 

118 

One of the Company’s startups  “Ohm Clean Tech Private Limited” had developed a 9 meter Hydrogen Fuel Cell bus which was flagged off by Honorable Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 6<sup>th</sup> February, 2023 at India Energy Week (IEW), Bengaluru. 

Startup Beta Tank Private Limited is developing a Robotic Tank cleaning system for cleaning Crude Oil Tank and retail tanks (like Diesel, Petrol etc). The have already patented the technology and Crude oil tanks cleaning robot got IECEx certificate for Zone zero operation. 

The Company supported innovative startups ‘Caliche Private Limited’ which has developed a biochemical technology for controlling sand influx in oil wells. As a result of Company’s support, the startup has secured a development order for deployment of its technology in three wells. Caliche is currently focused on the commercialization of its two flagship product lines: SandPax, a biochemical sand influx control technology, and CarbonOne, a microbial carbon capture technology. The Company is driving market adoption through direct customer engagements as well as strategic partnerships. 

Hopun Innovations Private Limited is a startup incubated at IIT Bhubaneswar and supported by the Company under its Startup Initiative. The startup develops indigenous electric utility vehicles for industrial and commercial applications. Under Company’s support, it successfully designed, developed, and delivered prototype electric vehicles few of which shall be very soon deployed for trial run (in-campus) in FHQ, Duliajan. The project demonstrated the startup’s technical capability and the potential of its electric mobility solutions to support Company’s sustainability and decarbonization initiatives. 

Another startup supported by the Company ‘Minimines’, operates in the field of lithium-ion battery recycling and resource recovery. The startup is developing sustainable recycling and extraction technologies to enable a circular economy for the electric vehicle ecosystem. Its carbon-neutral solutions focus on recovering valuable materials from end-of-life lithium-ion batteries, including cobalt, copper, nickel, aluminium, lithium, and graphite. Through these innovative technologies, Minimines aims to enhance resource efficiency, reduce environmental impact, and support the transition towards sustainable mobility. 

There are several other success stories under Company’s Startup Initiative. Through its startup programme, the Company has adopted a forward-looking approach to fostering innovation, nurturing entrepreneurship, and promoting sustainable technologies across diverse sectors. By supporting emerging innovators and indigenous solutions, the Company is contributing to the growth of the startup ecosystem while addressing industry challenges. Oil India Limited is proud to be associated with the country’s vibrant and prestigious startup ecosystem. 

# **19. Net Zero Pursuit** 

The Company is committed to achieve the 2040 Net Zero target and has demonstrated its commitment to transitioning into a clean and integrated energy Company aligning with the nation’s climate goals. As part of this Net Zero pursuit, the Company is implementing a structured, science-based roadmap to achieve net zero emissions by 2040, with interim targets of ~25% reduction by 2026, ~85% by 2030 and ~95% by 2035. Through Project SANTULAN, the Company operationalized 26 high-impact initiatives focused on GHG reduction, environmental sustainability and strategic enablers. The Company has committed an investment of approximately ` 20,000 crore towards key decarbonization levers, which include reduction of flaring, renewable energy, compressed biogas (CBG), green hydrogen, electrifying traditional gas fired equipment, CCS/CCUS, Geothermal, energy efficiency upgrades, energy storage solutions and Dynamic Gas Blending in Drilling Rigs. Through some of these implemented efforts, the Company has already achieved a further 17.93% reduction in emissions in FY 2025-26 over the base year FY 2023-24. The current Scope 1 and 2 emission figure is 1.190 MMT CO2e as against 1.268 MMT CO2e in the previous year. 

Achieving lower emissions through gas flaring reduction is an important lever to reduce emission for the oil and gas sector to meet the climate goals. The Company initiated zero routine flaring projects with a goal to reduce carbon emissions and monetise the flared gas by upgrading and construction of installations, adding pipelines to evacuate gas and installing compression facilities for gas field monetisation.  It is noteworthy that during FY 2025–26, the total gas flaring by the Company has been reduced to 56 MMSCM, as compared to 82 MMSCM in FY 2024–25, reflecting a reduction of approximately 32% in Assam and Arunachal Pradesh. 

119 



With Installed Renewable Energy Capacity of 188.1 MW, the Company is committed to deploying 5 - 5.5 gigawatts of renewable energy capacity by 2040, emphasizing wind, solar and other sustainable energy sources. The Company already has in place Collaboration with Assam Government for installation of 645 MW Solar Projects across Assam with 25 MW solar plant under construction in Namrup, Assam. Your Company is also actively pursuing installation of roof top solar plant and has installed 339 KWp roof top solar plants in FY 2025-26 and also plans to further install 570 Kwp of roof top solar across assets pan India. The total installed capacity of captive solar plants in the Company for internal consumption has increased to 2261 Kwp in FY 2025-26. The total captive solar power generation in the reporting year has also increased by 45.78% compared to the previous year. 

In line with the Government of India’s vision of advancing affordable and sustainable energy, the Company is progressing the establishment of 25 Compressed Biogas (CBG) plants, each with an output capacity of 2–5 Tonnes Per Day (TPD), across strategically selected locations in Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Tripura, West Bengal, Odisha, Jharkhand, Rajasthan, Himachal Pradesh and Haryana. This landmark green initiative underscores Company’s commitment to fostering a circular economy by transforming organic waste into clean, renewable energy, while contributing to effective waste management and creating lasting environmental and socio-economic benefits for communities across the country. 

Your Company has forged prominent collaboration with leading national international platforms to accelerate its sustainability and decarbonization journey.  As a signatory to the Oil and Gas Decarbonization Charter (OGDC), the Company has committed to industry wide collective action towards reducing greenhouse gas emissions and achieving net zero target. In pursuit to reduce GHG emissions, your Company has conducted a fugitive emission detection and quantification campaign through an agreement with TotalEnergies in its production installations.  The detection & quantification of Methane and Carbon dioxide was done through a drone-based survey using TotalEnergies proprietary AUSEA (Airborne Ultra-light Spectrometer for Environmental Applications) technology. 

Further, your Company through its material subsidiaryNRL has embarked on a journey to Green Hydrogen, which signifies our commitment to harnessing the potential of hydrogen as a clean and sustainable energy source. As part of this initiative a 2.4 KTPA of green 

hydrogen plant is currently being built and is expected to be commissioned by 2026.  The potential for reduction of CO2 emission will be 0.024 MMTPA. In strengthening its green portfolio, the Company, through NRL, has commissioned a 2G Ethanol plant based on bamboo feedstock, under the joint venture Assam Bio-Refinery Private Limited. 

Your Company in its pursuit towards the Net Zero has taken initiative to electrify operations through Green Energy.  Your Company has already connected 05 (five) installations in FHQ with green power to reduce scope 1 and 2 emissions.  Initiatives have also been taken to connect the Pump Stations: PS4, PS5, PS6 and PS7 pipeline stations with grid power.  Your Company will be connecting more installations to the grid to enable supply of renewable power to run the installations in future. 

The concept of Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) to enable large scale underground sequestration is gaining traction in view of drastic climate change. Identification of suitable storage complex for permanent storage of CO2 plays a major role in path towards decarbonization and net zero from the perspective of upstream Oil and Gas Sector. In this regard, your Company has conducted a feasibility study for identification of suitable reservoirs/aquifers along with design considerations for capture, transportation and sequestration of CO2 in suitable reservoirs/aquifers within Jaisalmer Basin in Rajasthan. Successful completion of the study will serve as a demonstration project and pave the way for CCUS deployment in India. 

The Company has taken the strategic initiative to venture into geothermal energy exploration in India, marking a significant step towards diversifying its energy portfolio. This move aligns with the Government India’s vision to promote the development of geothermal resources as a sustainable and reliable component of the country’s future energy mix. Recognizing the longterm potential of geothermal energy, the Company has identified it as a key focus area under its new energy initiatives and is actively undertaking measures to assess its viability and implement pilot scale projects. In this regard a collaborative Study with Centre for Earth Sciences & Himalayan Studies (CES & HS) and National Centre for Seismology (NCS), Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES), for Geothermal Potential in Arunachal Pradesh has been undertaken.  Also, the Company has initiated a feasibility study on extracting geothermal energy by repurposing of abandoned/to be abandoned oil and gas wells. 

120 

Your Company has taken various energy efficiency measures to reduce emissions.  Notable among these are replacement of conventional appliances in FHQ with energy efficient appliances across the Company resulting in savings of 2745.43 tCO2e in emissions. 

Electrical energy storage is one of the frontline solutions towards reducing emissions and your Company has taken an important step in this regard.  Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) is being explored to enhance energy reliability, grid stability and support renewable integration. 

Further, your Company is operating Dynamic Gas Blending (DGB) system in one Drilling Rig. The DGB system, allows diesel engines to operate on diesel and natural gas simultaneously, reducing environmental impact and operational cost, without compromising the engine performance.  This has resulted in direct reduction of emissions due to lower diesel consumption and the same will be extended to two more drilling rigs. 

The Company has registered 431 hectares of land across Assam and Odisha, under the Government of India’s Green Credit Program (GCP). Of this, plantation activities have already been undertaken in 431 hectares, putting the Company on track to earn green credits in 2029. These credits will help offset residual emissions and support India’s national afforestation goals. 

Through these multi-dimensional initiatives, the Company is not only reducing its environmental footprint but also creating a scalable and resilient clean energy model. The Company’s proactive approach underscores its leadership in India’s energy transition and reflects its commitment to delivering long-term value for stakeholders while contributing meaningfully to national and global climate goals.

# **Implementation of SAP S/4 HANA: Transforming Enterprise Operations** 

FY 2025–26 marked a defining milestone in the Company’s digital transformation journey with the successful migration from SAP ECC 6.0 to SAP S/4HANA on RISE with SAP. The transformation encompassed the implementation of a cloud-enabled digital core integrated with SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP), SAP Work Zone, SAP Fiori, SAP Cloud Platform Integration (CPI) and SAP BW/4HANA with BPC, creating a unified and future-ready enterprise platform. 

Following the successful deployment of SAP SRM, SAP S/4HANA and BW/4HANA, the Company achieved enterprise-wide Go-Live on 4 August 2025. This landmark achievement represents one of the most significant technology modernization initiatives undertaken by the Company, aimed at enhancing operational excellence, strengthening governance, and enabling data-driven decision-making across the enterprise. 

Built on SAP’s in-memory HANA technology and hosted on the RISE with SAP Private Cloud, the new ERP landscape has significantly enhanced business performance through faster transaction processing, streamlined workflows and real-time enterprise reporting. The transformation has established a single source of truth for Finance, Procurement, Human Resources, IS-OIL, Materials Management, Project Systems and other core business functions, enabling greater transparency, agility and control. 

The adoption of SAP Fiori, Work Zone and mobileenabled ERP services has substantially enhanced employee experience by providing intuitive, role-based and anytime-anywhere access to business processes. Digital self-service capabilities for employees and managers have accelerated Company’s journey toward a paperless and more efficient workplace. 

The transformation has delivered significant improvements in payroll processing, financial closing, invoice management and overall system responsiveness, while reducing process cycle times across the 

122 

enterprise. Real-time analytics and embedded reporting capabilities now empower leadership with timely insights for faster and more informed decision-making. 

Beyond immediate operational benefits, the new digital platform establishes a strong foundation for the adoption of emerging technologies including Artificial Intelligence, SAP Joule, intelligent automation, advanced analytics and future digital innovations. The cloud-based architecture enhances cybersecurity, business continuity, scalability and disaster recovery readiness while eliminating the complexities of managing on-premise infrastructure. 

More than a technology upgrade, SAP S/4HANA represents Company’s transition to an intelligent, integrated and digitally connected enterprise. By modernizing its core business systems and embracing a cloud-first digital strategy, Company has strengthened its capability to drive sustainable growth, operational resilience and innovation in an increasingly dynamic energy landscape. 

“The successful implementation of SAP S/4HANA is a strategic step towards building a future-ready OIL. It not only enhances operational efficiency and governance but also provides a robust digital foundation for innovation, agility and long-term value creation.” 

# **21.  Cyber Security - Strengthening Measures** 

Considering the persistent and evolving nature of cybersecurity threats for the Company, effective management and mitigation of such threats require sustained, organization-wide efforts and seamless coordination. 

To strengthen its cybersecurity posture, the organization has overhauled its Information Security Governance Structure to ensure cybersecurity considerations are strategically aligned with business objectives. 

As part of a comprehensive cybersecurity enhancement program, the organization has undertaken multiple initiatives. Specialized programs have been conducted for building the capabilities of core cybersecurity groups, regular cyber incident response drills are being conducted to test preparedness and refine response mechanisms under simulated attack scenarios. 

Despite its relatively recent foray into cybersecurity, the Company has taken ambitious initiatives in FY 2025-26, 

including strategic policy interventions, formalisation of all policies and procedures, comprehensive audit, establishment of a 24x7 ICT Security Operations Centre. Company has also started working on opportunities of improvements in the area of cybersecurity as identified during comprehensive Gap Assessment. The leadership’s unwavering commitment to safeguarding critical cyber infrastructure, particularly in the context of a volatile geopolitical environment, is demonstrated through proactive self-defence measures and stringent adherence to regulatory guidelines issued by CERTIn and NCIIPC. Your Company remains steadfast in its mission to protect its critical information infrastructure by conducting audits of key installations, which are vital not only to the organization but also to the nation’s energy security. The Company regards cybersecurity as a high-impact, high-materiality governance priority integral to its sustainability agenda. Cyber risk is meticulously monitored by the leadership, ensuring robust governance and oversight. These concerted efforts position your Company at par with its peers in India’s oil and gas sector, setting a strong foundation for an ambitious digital transformation underpinned by rigorous cybersecurity controls.

## **A. Conservation of Energy** 

Apart from being self-reliant to meet its energy requirement, Company has been trying to make the maximum use of natural gas as energy source thereby keeping the demand on refined petroleum products to bare minimum. 

The Company has taken up extensive programs for conservation of energy in different forms. While endeavour toward conservation of energy has been going on from very early stage of Company’s operations, measures have been constantly updated and reassessed for the same. Various short term and long-term measures towards conservation of energy adopted by the Company. 

### **i). Reduction in flaring of Natural Gas:** 

The Company’s continued focus on maximizing associated gas utilization and strengthening gas evacuation infrastructure resulted in a significant reduction in gas flaring during FY 2025–26, reinforcing its commitment to operational efficiency and environmental sustainability. 

During FY 2025–26, the total gas flaring by the Company has been reduced to 56 MMSCM, as compared to 82 MMSCM in FY 2024–25, reflecting a reduction of approximately 32 % in Assam and Arunachal Pradesh. This significant decline has been achieved through continuous and focused efforts to monetize associated gas by strengthening surface facilities, compression infrastructure and evacuation systems.

# **iii). Reduction in HSD/Petrol Consumption:** 

During FY 2025–26, Your Company implemented several initiatives to conserve diesel (HSD), crude oil, and other resources while improving operational efficiency across its operations. The GMS Department conserved water by implementing closed coolant circuits in 99 gas compressor packages, saving approximately 500 litres of water per compressor per day. The Logistics Department achieved a 16% reduction in HSD consumption through improved planning and optimized logistics operations. The Electrical Engineering Department is implementing solarpowered microgrid systems integrated with Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) across key installations, with plans for phased expansion to substantially reduce diesel consumption and strengthen the Company’s clean energy transition. The Pipeline Department expanded the use of grid and solar power, resulting in significant diesel savings, including 7,043 litres at ` -15, 5,674 litres 

at ` -14 (36.26% reduction), and 3,547 litres through grid power at ` -2, while solar power generation at PS-3 led to the conservation of 24.30 MT (27.77 KL) of crude oil. In Rajasthan, gas flaring was reduced to net zero, wells were grouped for efficient DG utilization, and SRP motors were downsized to optimize energy consumption. Additionally, KGB & MBP reduced diesel consumption during TCP operations by replacing a diesel-intensive hydraulic firing mechanism with a nitrogen-based mechanical firing system, enhancing both energy efficiency and resource conservation. 

# **iv). SAKSHAM - 2026:** 

As directed by Petroleum Conservation Research Association (PCRA), Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, Govt. of India, SAKSHAM 2025-26 was observed from 1<sup>st</sup> Feb 2026 to 15<sup>th</sup> Feb 2026. During this period various activities were organised including mass awareness drive seeking public to actively participate in fuel conservation for health & environmental protection and simultaneously help in reducing India’s dependency on import of crude oil. 

Throughout the event, various activities were organized, including a pledge-taking ceremony, awareness displays and quiz competitions, walkathon and cyclothon for public outreach, an expert talk on fuel conservation, and an emission check camp with media engagement. Additionally, social media posting of the events and schoollevel awareness programs played a vital role in spreading the message on climate change and sustainable energy practices.

# **B.  Technology Upgradation: Unlocking Untapped Potential** 

Your Company remains committed to accelerating the adoption of advanced and fit-for-purpose technologies 

across the entire hydrocarbon value chain—from exploration and field development to production optimisation, reservoir management, and asset integrity. To keep pace with emerging technological advancements, the Company continues to organise regular technology induction forums to evaluate innovative solutions with the potential to enhance operational efficiency, production performance, safety, and sustainability. In support of this initiative, a dedicated online technology portal enables reputed technology and service providers from India and abroad to register and submit proposals for innovative solutions across the Exploration, Development, and Production domains. The Company continues to receive encouraging responses from leading domestic and international technology providers and remains focused on fast-tracking the evaluation and deployment of promising technologies to strengthen operational excellence and drive long-term value creation. 

# **C. Technology Absorption:** 

## **Upgradation of High-Performance Computing Centre (HPCC)** 

Company’s High-Performance Computing Centre (HPCC) 2.0 christened as PRISM (Processing, Reservoir Imaging and Subsurface Modelling) was successfully commissioned at Duliajan. This marks a significant milestone as HPCC 2.0 is the first of its kind hybrid datacentre in India’s upstream E&P landscape to integrate both CPU and GPU architectures, delivering the computational power necessary for executing complex, data-intensive geophysical workflows. HPCC 2.0 will seamlessly manage vast volume of seismic data processing, interpretation and reservoir characterization studies. 

## **Installation of Drilling Simulator (DrillSim 5000)** 

A new state-of-the-art Drilling Simulator (DrillSim 5000) has been commissioned at the Institute of Well Control Technology (IWCT), Duliajan. The Institute is accredited to International Well Control Forum (IWCF), UK as a primary centre for conducting ‘Rotary Drilling Well Control Courses to strengthen the Company’s core competencies and capability in drilling while ensuring regulatory compliance and operational safety. 

## **Use of GeoAI during Reservoir Studies** 

GeoAI a module of Hampson Russell Software leverages rock physics to generate an extensive training data 

131 



catalog to train the convolutional neural network (CNN). It allows to fine-tune the trained CNN with real seismic data and the actual elastic property logs, thus enabling the CNN to accurately model elastic property variations and demonstrating a superior match with blind wells. GeoAI also enables effective porosity estimation, revealing favourable reservoir conditions. These capabilities enhance exploration decision-making and reduce risks, ultimately leading to more successful and efficient hydrocarbon exploration and production efforts. The module is being utilised during seismic inversion & reservoir characterization for optimal placement of drilling locations. 

## **Induction of Paleo-Scan for Seismic Data Interpretation** 

Company inducted PaleoScan™, the proprietary software from Eliis S.A.S. (France), in December 2025 to strengthen its geoscientific workflows, particularly for improved seismic interpretation, structural and stratigraphic analysis, fault and horizon mapping, and identification of subtle hydrocarbon prospects. The software supports accelerated seismic interpretation, extracts automated horizons and faults, identification of stratigraphic features and quantify geobodies for enhanced reservoir prediction and play-level exploration. The application software is being utilised extensively for deriving interpretative value from seismic data towards derisking and optimal placement of exploration and development locations. 

# **COEES :** 

## **i. CO2 Mineralization Reactor Setup:** 

A customized “CO2 Mineralization Reactor Setup” was developed at CoEES, Company in collaboration with Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur under a collaborative research project focused on investigating CO2 trapping mechanisms in saline aquifers in India. The reactor system comprises a 500 mL SS316 highpressure reactor cell designed to operate at pressures up to 280 bar and temperatures up to 250°C. The facility is intended for conducting CO2 mineralization studies on various subsurface rock samples under simulated reservoir conditions, enabling assessment of CO2 sequestration potential in saline aquifers as well as reactive basaltic formations. The establishment of this advanced experimental setup strengthens the research capabilities of CoEES, in the field of Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) and supports India’s Net Zero emission objectives. 

## **ii. HP-HT Contact Angle Goniometer:** 

The commissioning of a high-pressure, hightemperature (HP–HT) Contact Angle Goniometer at the EOR Laboratory, CoEES, represents a significant advancement in reservoir characterization and enhanced oil recovery (EOR) research. This sophisticated instrument enables precise measurement of interfacial tension (IFT) and contact angle under simulated reservoir conditions, facilitating accurate evaluation of fluid–fluid and rock–fluid interactions. The capability to assess wettability alteration of rock surfaces at elevated pressure and temperature is critical for designing efficient EOR strategies, particularly for complex reservoirs as well as for CCS related studies. The system enhances experimental reliability, supporting fundamental studies on capillary forces, phase behaviour, and surface chemistry. 

## **iii. HP-HT Rheometer:** 

The commissioning of a high-pressure, hightemperature (HP–HT) rheometer at the EOR Laboratory, CoEES, marks a significant milestone in technological absorption for advanced fluid characterization. This instrument enables precise measurement of viscosity and rheological behaviour of brines, crude oils, and various chemical solutions under simulated reservoir conditions. Such capability is essential for understanding non-Newtonian flow characteristics, shear-dependent viscosity, and thermal stability of EOR fluids. The system facilitates optimization of injection strategies, improves predictive modelling of fluid flow in porous media, and enhances design of chemical formulations for improved oil recovery in challenging HP–HT reservoir environments. 

Some other initiatives of the Company are highlighted below : 

- The Company has initiated action towards addressing sand related issues in its fields. Chemical Sand Consolidation is an emergent technology in handling sand related issues in wells and thereby optimally produce from such wells. The technology has been brought in for application in its wells in Assam & Arunachal Fields. 

- With the intent to produce from multiple zones at a time from the company’s fields in Upper Assam, installation of multizone completion string has been initiated. With this initiative, the Company is focusing on enhancing production from its mature fields. 

132 

- A number of wells in the Company’s Upper Assam fields could not be previously brought into production due to very high pour point and asphaltene containing crude oil. To monetise these wells, the company has successfully executed specialized chemical injection in the downhole and thereby established production in some of the wells. This initiative emphasises the Company’s focus on producing from such wells having high pour point and asphaltene characteristics in the coming years. 

- Liquidation of sick well is one of the primary activities of an E&P company. Sick well revival provides a significant contribution towards arresting the decline rate of matured fields of the Company and for enhancing crude oil production. With a view to liquidate sick wells rapidly and maximize workover gain, the Company carried out another campaign of study of wells during the year. 

- The company brought Digital Transformation in its entire fleet of Crude oil tankers (bowsers) operating in Assam & Arunachal Fields through BoLD (Bowser Logistics Digitalization) initiative. Some of the benefits derived from BoLD are reduced cost-to-serve through improved asset utilization, faster process Turn-Around-Time (TAT), enhanced manpower productivity, digitization of data at source and greater transparency in overall process. 

- The company embarked on a first-of-its-kind Dronebased “Methane and Carbon Dioxide emissions detection and measurement” campaign in its Production Installations in Upper Assam fields using Total Energies’ pioneer AUSEA (Air borne Ultralight Spectrometer for Environmental Applications) technology. The AUSEA campaign marks an important step in strengthening the company’s decarbonization efforts and Net Zero commitments. 

- **Multi-casing Thickness Detector:** The tool, which helps in Quantitative determination of Corrosion and total metal loss in 3 concentric Tubulars-   2 7/8” tubing, 5 1/2” casing and 9 5/8” casing, eliminates the need to pull out tubing for its operation and can operate in rigless environment, thereby saving considerable time and cost of the well. 

- **Downhole video:** This tool provides real time view of wellbore enabling assessment of downhole fish, leak, tubular corrosion, tubular damage, perforation inspection, GLV inspection etc thereby helping to diagnose the complicated downhole condition of 

   - the wells and effectively assist during workover operations of Oil and Gas Wells. 

- **Noise tool:** This tool identifies the source of water entry, abnormal fluid movement, Crossflow detection between wellbore and formation or channel behind the casing. It can also detect leak in Packer/Plug/Tubular. 

- **Application of Stim gun with Deep connect charges:** Stim gun assisted perforation using 3.3/8” TAG-Deep connect charges to deliver greater penetration than conventional perforating charges. Propellant-based explosives dynamically clean and stimulates the near well bore area enhancing flow. 

- **3D Resistivity:** Induction resistivity tool which can measure resistivity in 3 axes. Applications include identification & quantification of hydrocarbon in thinly bedded sand shale sequences. 

- **Core-flood set-up/Core Flooding System:** This is a state-of-the-art equipment with automated design to perform both Steady state and Unsteadystate relative permeability measurements both at reservoir and ambient conditions. The system is being customized in such a way that the same can be compatible for core flooding experiments using various fluids viz. brines with varying salinity, polymers, surfactants, Carbon Di-oxide (CO2) gas, mineral oil, live crude oil, dead crude oil, N2 gas etc. experiments. 

- **Digital Microscope (Make:** EVIDENT-OLYMPUS, Japan, Model No: DSX1000): The digital microscope is an essential equipment in the newly established corrosion laboratory, designed to facilitate detailed analysis of corrosion in oilfield tubular components and wellhead fittings. This advanced high-precision imaging system allows for the examination of both uniform and localized corrosion including pitting, crevice and intergranular corrosion under low magnification without requiring surface polishing, thereby preserving sample integrity. As a non-destructive evaluation (NDE) tool, it supports accurate failure analysis while maintaining the original state of the samples. 

- **Procurement of New Generation Chemicals in Water Based Mud System:** “While drilling high-angle deviated wells in Eocene formations, challenges like high torque, drag, stuck pipe, and hole washout were encountered. To mitigate these, the Chemical Department optimized the drilling fluid system, 

133 



emphasizing improved shale inhibition and lubricity. Premium chemicals such as Polyamine, EP Lube, graphene-based lubricants, and Potassium Sulphate were introduced to enhance performance.” 

- **Field implementation of Nano-polymer products in Water Based Mud systems:** These eco-friendly, nano-sized products enhance water-based mud systems by improving hole cleaning, reducing ECD, increasing ROP, and minimizing downhole issues. They offer multi-functional benefits—such as shale stabilization, fluid loss control, and bit balling prevention—while replacing five conventional rigsite chemicals.” 

- **Landmark Software:** Drilling in complex formations involves challenges like shale reactivity, wellbore instability, and pressure variations. To address these, the Chemical Department adopted Landmark Software with the Well Plan suite for real-time analysis of mud hydraulics, surge and swab pressures, and well control. This digital tool aids in efficient decision-making, improved hole cleaning, pressure management, and optimized circulation with reduced formation damage. 

- Online Real time Monitoring System of Drilling operation is fully functional and all Rigs are monitored currently including Live data from Andaman Offshore, Jodhpur and Mahanadi. This monitoring system provides real time access to the well data in customized screens for easy use which helps to understand the behaviour of the well and allows the operational team to take informed decisions 24x 7. Additionally, predictive analytics are being carried out for better well management. 

- State-of-the-art high end LWD (Logging While Drilling) technology is being deployed there by reducing dependency on Wireline log post drilling in complex well where there are operational down hole issues. 

- **Stab -In Cementing:** The Cementing Section introduced Stab-In Cementing for 20” casing, reducing reliance on precise hole volume estimates and minimizing cement contamination. By allowing pumping until surface returns, the method improves displacement efficiency and cement bond quality, enhancing overall well integrity. 

- **DOC (Diesel Oxidation Catalysts):** To reduce particulate emissions from Powerpack Engines on 

drilling rigs, a Diesel Oxidation Catalyst (DOC) has been installed. This platinum-coated system oxidizes carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons, and organic particulates into CO2 and water, significantly lowering the environmental impact of exhaust emissions. 

- Dynamic Gas Blending after successful implementation at S#7 Rig Engines, Dynamic Gas Blending (DGB) additional kit is being proposed for more Rig Engines. 

- **Propellent Stimulation:** Propellant stimulation has been introduced to enhance production from tight reservoirs, yielding a significant gain and it has been carried out in 5 wells. This technique uses solid rocket fuel cartridges deployed via E-Line, which detonate at target depth to generate pressure pulses that fracture surrounding rock, improving hydrocarbon flow. 

- **Hydro-Frac:** Current Hydro-frac campaign in the Company is being executed and a total of 09 wells were successfully hydro fractured during the financial year 2025-2026 through the engagement of specialized hired service providers. 

- **Radial Drilling:** Radial drilling contract has been carried out in 03 no of wells in FY 2025-26. 

- **Single String Multi-zone Completion:** Single String Multizone Completion enables sequential testing and production of multiple reservoirs  through a single wellbore, without requiring a workover rig. It allows selective or commingled production from different zones, offering a rigless and efficient solution for multi-reservoir exploitation. This technology has been deployed in well no. Dinjan#01 in Company’s upper Assam fields during FY 2025-26. 

- **Successful Installation & Testing of Compact Well-Head:** This advanced wellhead system integrates casing hangers, seals, and lockdown mechanisms into a compact design, reducing size, weight, and complexity. It streamlines installation, accommodates various casing requirements, and minimizes time, leak paths, risks, and costs during drilling operations. 

- **Introduction of new fishing tools:** Introduced new fishing tools like Packer milling & Retrieval tool and Superficial Jar in the workover operation to recovery of Fish. 

134 

- **Innovation Factori Solutions (Well Portfolio Optimizer):** This innovative technology leverages AI/ML for production optimization and reservoir management. The WPO prototype integrates hardware and software to standardize data, screen and rank wells, identify issues, recommend interventions, and predict production gains along with success probabilities.” The technology has been deployed in 150 wells of Company’s Upper Assam fields in FY 2025-26. 

- **Thru Tubing Acid Simulation Tool (STIMSTIXX):** This acid stimulation tool shall be wireline-deployed to enhance production in oil and gas wells by removing near-wellbore damage such as scale and fines accumulation. The stimulation shall involve the use of wireline-deployed (Thru-Tubing) chemical treatment tools that deliver acid stimulation directly to the target zone treating perforations, screens, or gravel packs. The near wellbore stimulation treatment is intended to improve the production in both new and existing perforations. 

- **Introduction of Snubbing unit for Workover Operation:** A snubbing unit offers significant operational, economic and environmental advantages over a conventional workover rig, as it enables well intervention under pressure without the need for killing the well, thereby avoiding the cost, time and environmental risks associated with procuring, handling, disposing and recovering kill fluids. It minimizes formation damage caused by nonnative fluids and helps maintain reservoir conditions conducive to sustained or improved production. Its compact and portable configuration permits quicker rig-up and rig-down, faster tripping, while also enabling well testing. Further, the unit provides enhanced operational flexibility, including rotation of the work string under pressure and independent BOP accumulator systems, while reducing water requirement, surface disturbance and overall environmental footprint, particularly in sensitive locations. The unit is under procurement and is expected to be operational by end of FY 2026-27.

# **D. Technology Absorption through R&D** 

The Research and Development team of the company has consistently been focusing on delivering innovative, cost-effective, and practically feasible solutions to tackle the persistent issues faced in our oilfields over the last four decades. The Company has also partnered with IITs / CSIR / Universities and Research institutes to leverage academic research. These collaborations help Company in accessing cutting-edge technology and expertise. Details of some of important studies undertaken / achievements during the FY 2025-26 are as under: 

## **(i) R&D** 

## **i. Development of Nanomaterials for Oil and Gas Applications** 

Microemulsion formulations were developed and optimized for enhanced residual oil recovery applications. The formulations were subjected to comprehensive laboratory evaluation, including interfacial tension (IFT) measurements and core flooding experiments conducted subsequent to water flooding, to assess their displacement efficiency and recovery performance. The experimental results demonstrated significant effectiveness of the developed formulations in mobilizing residual oil. Based on the encouraging laboratory outcomes, the necessary scale-up studies for field implementation are currently underway. 

## **ii. Production of Bio-hydrogen from produced / waste water** 

Extensive experimentation during 2025-26 enabled the research team to optimise a biohydrogen production technique by using indigenous microbes in culture media comprising of agricultural wastes and wastewater. The research has been able to achieve a hydrogen concentration of around 80% v/v in the gas produced using novel microbes which indicates towards a viable wasteto-energy pathway. This pioneering initiative, which is aligned with the Company’s Vision 2040, reinforces the Company’s strategic priorities of Energy Transition, Sustainability, and Indigenous R&D. A prototype was developed and demonstrated in IEW 2026 held in Goa. 

## **iii. Development of Green Spotting Fluid to release Differential Stuck Pipe encountered in drilling operations** 

Studies were undertaken to develop an environmentally sustainable green spotting fluid for the remediation of differential stuck pipe incidents in the Company’s drilling operations. Laboratory investigations revealed that a blend of oxidizing agents in a Lightweight Microbubble Fluid effectively degrades polymer-rich mud cakes under reservoir conditions. The study establishes a cost-effective and eco-friendly alternative to conventional oil-based spotting fluids and provides a strong foundation for future field-scale implementation to mitigate and release differential stuck pipe situations. 

## **iv. Development of noble material for efficient capture and conversion of CO2 into Green Fuels via Artificial Photosynthesis** 

A cost-effective, energy-efficient, and sustainable material has been developed for efficient atmospheric CO2 capture and hydrogen generation through solar-driven water splitting. The developed material subsequently functions as a catalyst for the conversion of captured CO2 into methanol. A laboratory-scale prototype integrating the complete process chain - from CO2 capture to methanol production is being developed. Further process optimization is currently underway to enhance methanol selectivity and achieve higher production yields. 

## **v. Geomechanical study of rock samples using Triaxial system** 

The Geo-mechanics Laboratory equipped with newly procured Tri-axial system provides critical insights into mechanical behaviour of the reservoir through detailed analysis of rocks. By studying stress-strain relationships and various mechanical characteristics of subsurface formations, the facility enables more accurate wellbore stability assessments and optimized drilling designs. This further helps in minimizing operational risks and improve overall drilling efficiency. Furthermore, the laboratory is capable supporting advanced applications such as hydraulic fracturing design, fracture propagation studies, and enhanced oil recovery planning. 

136 

# **vi. Asphaltene structure elucidation using Field Emission – Scanning Electron Microscope (FE-SEM)** 

The structure of the asphaltene can be inferred from newly procured FE-SEM analysis in conjunction with XRD data. The XRD results suggest the presence of comparatively shorter and less condensed aromatic layers with a relatively ordered stacking arrangement. This interpretation is further corroborated by the FE-SEM images, which show a more regular and well-aligned stacking of aromatic sheets in certain samples. In contrast, such organized stacking behaviour was not observed in asphaltenes isolated from other crude oil samples, where the aromatic domains appear more irregular, disordered, and structurally heterogeneous. Therefore, FE-SEM can serve as an effective analytical tool for understanding the structural characteristics and associated physicochemical properties of asphaltenes. 

# **(ii)  COEES, Guwahati** 

# **i. Carbon Capture & Sequestration (CCS):** 

A feasibility study was undertaken to address one of the most critical challenges in Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS)—the safe and permanent geological sequestration of CO2. The study identified a suitable candidate site within the Jaisalmer Basin of Rajasthan for long-term underground storage of captured CO2. This initiative marks an important milestone in the development of India’s practical CCS capability and supports Company’s commitment to achieving Net Zero emissions by 2040, while also contributing to India’s national Net Zero target by 2070. 

The project envisages capturing CO2 from the natural gas production stream at Company’s Dandewala Gas Field through a membrane-based gas sweetening system. The separated CO2 will be compressed and injected into deep saline aquifers at an approximate depth of 3,000 metres for permanent geological storage. 

Following a comprehensive technical evaluation of storage security, caprock integrity, reservoir injectivity, containment efficiency, and long-term 

performance, the Baisakhi–Bedesir Formation was identified as the most suitable reservoir for pilotscale implementation. The formation is estimated to possess a storage capacity of approximately 4.6 to 7.1 million tonnes of CO . 2 

To assess storage performance and containment integrity, detailed reservoir simulations were conducted covering a 25-year injection period at a rate of 210 tonnes of CO2 per day, followed by 200 years of post-injection monitoring. The simulation results provide strong confidence in the long-term stability, security, and permanence of CO2 storage within the selected formation. 

Although modest in scale compared to several international commercial CCS facilities, this project represents a significant first step towards establishing indigenous CCS expertise, infrastructure, operational capabilities, and regulatory frameworks under Indian geological and climatic conditions. As India progresses toward large-scale CCS deployment, the experience and knowledge gained from this pilot project will serve as valuable building blocks for future projects across the country. The outcomes are expected to contribute significantly to greenhouse gas mitigation efforts and support the Indian oil and gas industry’s broader transition towards a lowcarbon and net-zero future. 

# **ii. Quantifying the trapping mechanisms for CO2 geo-storage in saline aquifers of Rajasthan, India:** 

CoEES, in collaboration with Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur, conducted a research study to evaluate the feasibility of Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) in the saline aquifers of Rajasthan, India. The study investigated CO2–brine–rock interactions through comprehensive geochemical laboratory analyses to assess the long-term stability and containment potential of injected CO2. The research further quantified the major CO2 trapping mechanisms, including structural, residual, solubility, and mineral trapping, relevant to the targeted saline aquifer formations. The findings provided valuable insights into the suitability and storage security of these reservoirs for long-term geological sequestration of CO2. 

137 



## **iii. Geothermal Energy exploration:** 

As part of its clean energy diversification strategy, the Company is expanding into the geothermal energy sector through collaborations with global experts, academic institutions, state and central government agencies, along with strengthening in-house capacity-building initiatives. Key collaborations and partnerships include the Centre for Earth Sciences & Himalayan Studies and Assam Power Distribution Company Limited. The Company is currently assessing geothermal prospects in the hot springs of Arunachal Pradesh through geological, geochemical, and geophysical investigations, while also evaluating the feasibility of repurposing abandoned oil and gas wells in the Upper Assam Basin for geothermal extraction. 

## **iv. Critical Mineral Exploration:** 

The Company has diversified into the critical minerals sector and become the first Indian oil and gas PSU to enter critical mineral exploration. The Company participated in the Critical Minerals Auctions under Tranches IV, V, and VI conducted by the Ministry of Mines, and emerged as the preferred bidder for the Phop Graphite & Vanadium Block in Arunachal Pradesh (Tranche IV) and the Jorkian-Satipura-Khunja Amalgamated Potash & Halite Block in Rajasthan (Tranche V). The blocks are currently in active exploration 

phase. The Company in collaboration with MECL, CSIR, and Indian Bureau of Mines plans to carry out exploration, beneficiation, EIA, and hydrogeological studies in these blocks. Internationally, the Company is also pursuing critical mineral opportunities in few of the prospective countries, supported by strategic partnerships with entities such as KABIL, International Resource Holdings, and YPF S.A. to strengthen its critical minerals value chain.

# **MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS REPORT** 

## **1. FY2025–26 IN PERSPECTIVE** 

FY2025–26 marked a defining year in Oil India Limited’s journey of strengthening its position as an integrated energy company while expanding its capabilities to meet the opportunities of a rapidly evolving energy landscape. Despite a year characterised by geopolitical uncertainty, commodity price volatility and supply-chain disruptions, the Company demonstrated resilience by simultaneously strengthening its core hydrocarbon business while accelerating investments in long-term growth engines. 

The year witnessed record levels of capex deployment, drilling activity, workover operations and pipeline transportation, reflecting a decisive shift towards capacity creation rather than short-term optimisation. These investments not only reinforced the Company’s production capabilities but also laid the foundation for sustainable production growth, reserve accretion and enhanced energy security. 

During the year, the Company achieved significant milestones across its strategic priorities. Exploration efforts expanded into frontier basins, resulting in new hydrocarbon discoveries and strengthening confidence in India’s unexplored sedimentary basins. Operational excellence was reflected through record drilling performance, improved production efficiency and sustained reserve replacement. Simultaneously, major downstream infrastructure, including the expansion of Numaligarh Refinery’s logistics ecosystem, further strengthened the Company’s integrated energy value chain. 

FY2025–26 also represented an important inflection point in the Company’s diversification journey. The incorporation of OIL Green Energy Limited (OGEL), continued development of compressed biogas projects, entry into critical minerals exploration and advancement of low-carbon technologies reaffirmed the Company’s commitment to building a balanced energy portfolio aligned with India’s long-term energy transition objectives. 

The Company’s strategy during the year was guided by a clear principle **to strengthen today’s business while building tomorrow’s energy enterprise.** This balanced approach enabled the Company to continue creating 

long-term value for shareholders while reinforcing its role in supporting India’s energy security, industrial growth and sustainability ambitions.

# **Management Perspective: Creating Value Through Disciplined Growth** 

For India, where energy demand continues to grow alongside rapid economic development, strengthening domestic hydrocarbon production while investing in emerging energy businesses has become a strategic national priority. Against this evolving landscape, the Company continues to pursue a disciplined growth strategy that balances operational excellence, financial resilience and long-term value creation. 

While softer crude oil prices moderated earnings during FY2025–26, the Company remained firm in its conviction that long-term value creation cannot be compromised by short-term commodity cycles. Accordingly, the Company continued to accelerate investments across exploration, field development, production infrastructure, refining, pipeline expansion and emerging energy businesses, laying a strong foundation for sustainable growth. 

During FY2025–26, the Group deployed a capital expenditure of ` 21,673.75 crore, including ` 8,439.90 crore towards the expansion of Numaligarh Refinery Limited, representing one of the largest investment programmes in the Company’s history. These investments were directed towards expanding production capacity, strengthening reserve sustainability, enhancing infrastructure and creating future growth platforms, while reinforcing the Company’s evolution from a conventional upstream producer into an integrated energy enterprise. 

Exploration and Production (E&P) continues to remain the cornerstone of the Company’s business and the principal driver of long-term value creation. At a time when several mature producing assets across the industry are witnessing natural production decline, the Company remains among the very few exploration and production companies in India, including private E&P companies to consistently pursue growth in both crude oil and natural gas production through disciplined exploration, accelerated field development, technologyenabled reservoir management and enhanced recovery initiatives. This strategic approach assumes even greater significance in supporting India’s objective of enhancing domestic energy security. 

The Company’s commitment to strengthening its core business was reflected in several landmark operational achievements during the year. The Company recorded its highest-ever drilling performance of 74 wells, comprising 22 exploratory and 52 development wells, resulting in two oil discoveries in Assam and one gas discovery in the Andaman Basin. The Company also achieved a Reserve Replacement Ratio (RRR) of 1.02, supported by an addition of 6.232 MMTOE of 2P reserves, reaffirming the sustainability of its resource base and future production potential. Operational excellence was further demonstrated through the highest daily crude oil production in fourteen years of 10,566 MTPD and the highest-ever crude oil pipeline transportation of 7.453 MMT, reflecting improved asset utilisation, operational reliability and execution excellence across the hydrocarbon value chain. As on 31 March 2026, the Company had three offshore drilling rigs under operation in the Andaman, Krishna-Godavari and Kerala-Konkan Basins, further strengthening its exploration footprint in India’s frontier offshore acreages. 

Alongside strengthening its core hydrocarbon business, the Company continued its transformation into an integrated energy enterprise. The ongoing expansion

of Numaligarh Refinery Limited, supported by the 1,635 km Paradip–Numaligarh Crude Oil Pipeline, is enhancing integration across exploration, transportation, refining and logistics, enabling the Company to capture greater value across the energy chain while improving operational resilience and long-term competitiveness.

The Company also invested ` 173.22 crore in Research & Development, representing 3.20% of Profit Before Tax, while filing five patent applications, reflecting its continued emphasis on technology-led productivity, operational excellence and innovation-driven growth. 

Beyond its core upstream business, the Company continues to strengthen a diversified portfolio across the energy value chain to enhance long-term resilience and create multiple avenues for growth. During FY2025– 26, the Company continued to support the expansion of Numaligarh Refinery Limited (NRL) towards a 9 MMTPA integrated refining complex, and 1,635 km Paradip– Numaligarh Crude Oil Pipeline (PNCPL), which would significantly strengthened crude logistics and feedstock security. The Company also advanced its presence in the City Gas Distribution (CGD) business, expanding its downstream footprint closer to end consumers. Internationally, the Company continued to optimise value from its producing assets in Mozambique and Russia through prudent capital allocation, operational efficiencies and disciplined cost optimisation, while pursuing selective overseas opportunities aligned with its long-term growth strategy. Together, these initiatives are strengthening the Company’s position as a diversified integrated energy company with balanced exposure across upstream, midstream, downstream and international businesses. 

Recognising that hydrocarbons will continue to remain an integral part of India’s energy mix even as cleaner energy sources gain prominence, the Company is pursuing a balanced and pragmatic energy transition strategy. During FY2025–26, the Company incorporated OIL Green Energy Limited (OGEL) as a wholly owned subsidiary to drive its new-energy initiatives, continued the development of 25 Compressed Biogas (CBG) projects across nine States, with four Municipal Solid Waste-based CBG plants under construction, and became the first Indian oil and gas PSU to enter the critical minerals sector through successful allocation of graphite-vanadium and potash-halite blocks. These initiatives are creating new growth engines while complementing the Company’s established exploration and production business. 

Technology, innovation and digital transformation continue to be key enablers of the Company’s future competitiveness. During the year, the Company launched DRIVE 2.0, comprising 10 Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Generative AI-enabled initiatives across the 

Sustainability remains embedded within the Company’s long-term business strategy. During FY2025–26, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions reduced by 17.93% over the FY2024 baseline, while Project SANTULAN, with an estimated investment of approximately ` 20,000 crore, continued to advance the Company’s Net Zero aspiration by 2040. These initiatives reinforce the Company’s commitment to responsible growth, environmental stewardship and alignment with India’s broader climate commitments. 

The Company’s disciplined approach to growth is equally reflected in its financial stewardship. Despite a challenging commodity price environment, the Company reported Standalone Total Income of ` 24,038.58 crore and Consolidated Total Income of ` 38,980.70 crore, while maintaining the highest domestic credit ratings of CRISIL AAA and CARE AAA, sovereign-equivalent international ratings from Moody’s (Baa3) and Fitch (BBB-), and recommending a total dividend of ` 11.50 per equity share. This reflects Management’s commitment to balancing strategic investments with financial discipline, balance sheet strength and sustainable shareholder returns. 

# **2. ECONOMIC SCENARIO & INDUSTRY ANALYSIS** 

## **Global Economic Scenario** 

The global economic landscape in 2025 was marked by significant policy shifts, heightened uncertainty and evolving trade dynamics. A substantial part of this volatility arose from changes in United States policy priorities, particularly the introduction of tariff measures that raised United States tariff rates to their highest levels in a century. Although subsequent trade agreements and tariff adjustments moderated some of these increases, tariff levels remained substantially above those prevailing in 2024. 

Global economic activity demonstrated resilience during 2025 despite higher trade barriers and policy uncertainty. Prior to the outbreak of conflict in the Middle East, the global economy had performed better 

148 

than anticipated, leading to upward revisions in growth forecasts. Global growth reached an annualised rate of 3.9% in the fourth quarter of 2025. 

The conflict in the Middle East has, however, introduced an additional challenge to the global outlook. Assuming that the conflict remains contained in both duration and intensity, global growth is projected to moderate to 3.1% in 2026 before improving marginally to 3.2% in 2027. Global inflation is expected to increase slightly in 2026 and subsequently resume its downward trajectory in 2027. The effects of slower growth and higher inflation are expected to be more pronounced in emerging market and developing economies. 

# **Indian Economic Scenario** 

India’s growth outlook for 2025 was revised upward by 1.0 percentage point from the October estimate to 7.6%, reflecting stronger-than-anticipated economic performance during the second and third quarters of the fiscal year and continued robust momentum in the fourth quarter. 

For 2026, the growth forecast was revised upward by 0.3 percentage point, including an increase of 0.1 percentage point from the January projection, to 6.5%. The revision reflects the positive spillover effects of the strong performance in 2025 and the reduction in additional US tariffs on Indian exports from 50% to 10%. These favourable developments are expected to more than offset the adverse effects arising from the conflict in the Middle East. Economic growth is projected to remain steady at 6.5% in 2027. 

Despite global uncertainties arising from the Middle East conflict and disruptions in energy markets, India’s economy is projected to maintain growth of 6.5% in FY2026–27, supported by resilient domestic fundamentals. Private consumption is expected to remain a key growth driver, aided by the GST rate reductions introduced in September 2025, which are expected to mitigate inflationary pressures and support household purchasing power. Continued fiscal discipline is also expected to strengthen macroeconomic stability, while targeted subsidies provide support to vulnerable sectors. 

India’s investment outlook remains positive, supported by a sound financial system, continued infrastructure development and policy measures aimed at improving the business environment. Merchandise exports are 

expected to benefit from the easing of US tariffs and the implementation of new free trade agreements, particularly with the European Union. Manufacturing sectors, including electronics, automobiles and other tradable goods, are expected to continue expanding, supported by government initiatives and increasing export opportunities. 

Figure: Sectoral contribution to industry growth, FY2023–24 to FY2025–26 



Over the medium term, assuming that energy-market and supply-chain disruptions normalise by late 2026, India’s economic growth is projected to accelerate and average 7.1% during FY2027–28 and FY2028–29. Strong domestic demand, resilient services exports, increasing trade openness, policy support for strategic sectors and micro, small and medium enterprises, and continued manufacturing growth are expected to support India’s position among the world’s fastest-growing major economies. 

# **Oil & Gas Sector: Global Scenario** 

Global energy demand continued to increase in 2025, resulting in higher consumption across all major energy sources. Electricity demand grew strongly across multiple sectors, while renewable energy deployment reached record levels and accounted for more than 70% of the additional electricity required. At the same time, consumption of all fossil fuels also increased, contributing to a new record high in global energyrelated carbon dioxide emissions. 

Energy policies continued to evolve across major economies. The United States strengthened support for domestic fossil fuel production and nuclear power while 

149 



reducing incentives for wind, solar and electric vehicles. In parallel, several countries introduced policy measures aimed at strengthening energy security amid growing concerns over supply reliability and geopolitical risks. 

The installed costs of renewable energy technologies, including solar photovoltaic, onshore wind and offshore wind, are expected to continue declining, alongside further reductions in battery-storage costs. The pace and extent of these reductions are expected to vary across countries, regions and scenarios, reflecting differences in existing cost structures, market conditions and global deployment trajectories. 

OPEC and its allies are expected to continue adopting a calibrated approach to production during 2026–27, balancing gradual supply increases with the objective of maintaining market stability. While additional production is expected to support recovering demand, prevailing market expectations suggest that crude oil prices are likely to remain under moderate pressure amid continued economic and geopolitical uncertainty. 

Global oil demand is forecast to increase by 2.5 million barrels per day between 2024 and 2030, reaching a plateau of approximately 105.5 million barrels per day by the end of the decade, followed by a marginal decline in 2030. This outlook reflects below-trend economic growth amid global trade tensions and fiscal imbalances, as well as the accelerating substitution of oil in the transport and power-generation sectors. 

Figure: World oil demand trends 

Oil demand in emerging and developing economies is expected to increase by 4.2 million barrels per day during 2024–2030, in contrast with a continued contraction in advanced economies. Asian markets are expected to account for the majority of this growth, with India’s projected increase of 1 million barrels per day representing the largest increase for any single country. 

World oil production capacity is forecast to rise by 5.1 million barrels per day to 114.7 million barrels per day by 2030, led by Saudi Arabia and the United States. This increase is expected to significantly exceed the projected rise of 2.5 million barrels per day in global oil demand over the same period. 

Global natural gas liquids production is expected to increase by 2.3 million barrels per day to 20.1 million barrels per day by 2030, accounting for nearly half of the projected increase in world oil production capacity. A strategic focus on natural gas development by producers in the Middle East is expected to increase regional natural gas liquids supply by 1.4 million barrels per day by 2030. 

# **Oil & Gas Sector: Indian Scenario Crude Oil and Refining** 

India’s significance in global oil markets is projected to increase considerably over the remainder of the decade, supported by robust economic expansion, a rising population and favourable demographic trends. The global energy crisis has elevated energy security as a major policy priority, which is particularly relevant for India given its heavy reliance on imported crude oil to meet domestic energy requirements. 



India is projected to be the largest contributor to global oil-demand growth through 2030. Driven by rapid industrialisation and economic expansion, diesel and gasoil are expected to be the primary drivers of this increase, accounting for nearly half of the country’s additional oil demand. India is also expected to contribute more than one-sixth of the total increase in global oil demand through 2030. 

India is currently the world’s third-largest energy consumer. Its oil demand, estimated at around 4.6 million barrels per day, is projected to increase to approximately 6.64 million barrels per day by 2030. At the same time, domestic crude oil production has been declining gradually, resulting in growing dependence on imports, which currently account for nearly 89% of the country’s oil requirements.
