# **Company’s Strategic Approach to an Evolving Energy Landscape** 

To meet projected demand, India plans to further expand its LNG infrastructure. Several terminals are under construction or at the planning stage, with the potential to add nearly 40 billion cubic metres per year of regasification capacity by 2030. 

India’s domestic gas production has recorded a resurgence. Total net gas production reached 35 billion cubic metres in 2023, meeting approximately half of the country’s gas demand. This growth was primarily driven by deepwater fields in the Krishna–Godavari Basin, which now account for nearly 25% of India’s total gas production. 

Between 2024 and 2030, domestic gas production is expected to record moderate growth, supported by increasing onshore production from Coal Bed Methane (CBM) and Discovered Small Fields (DSF). 

The Government of India has set a target of increasing the share of natural gas in the country’s energy mix to 15% by 2030, compared with 6.4% in 2022. This target has established the direction for supportive government policies aimed at increasing the use of natural gas in India’s energy economy. 

As a Maharatna public sector undertaking, Oil India is pursuing a balanced growth strategy to address the evolving challenges and opportunities presented by the global energy landscape. While continuing to strengthen its core exploration and production business, the Company is focused on production enhancement, reserve accretion, technology adoption, value-chain integration and diversification into emerging energy businesses. 

The execution of this strategy is supported by sustained capital deployment across the Company’s portfolio. During FY2025–26, the Company recorded its highestever capital expenditure utilisation of ` 13,025.51 crore, representing 186% of the revised estimate target. Capital deployment during the year was primarily directed towards accelerated exploration and development drilling, expanded seismic acquisition programmes, production infrastructure and pipeline projects, and strategic investments in subsidiaries and joint ventures. 

The Company’s strategic approach is articulated across the following five priorities: 

# **Strengthening Core E&P Operations** 

The Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board has authorised the establishment of a 33,592-kilometre natural gas pipeline network across the country, with the objective of creating a National Gas Grid under the 

To sustain and enhance hydrocarbon production, the Company is intensifying exploration, development drilling and workover activities across its producing assets. It is also deploying advanced Enhanced Oil 

152 

Recovery techniques, digital reservoir-management tools and innovative production technologies to improve recovery from mature and declining fields. 

During FY 2025–26, these efforts contributed to the Company recording its highest-ever daily oil and gas production of 1,49,360 BOEPD on 31 March 2026, including record daily crude oil production of 81,354 BOPD. The Company also completed a record 307 workover jobs and successfully drilled 74 wells, while drilling meterage increased by 41.5% over the previous year. 

# **Reserve Accretion and Frontier Exploration** 

The Company is accelerating exploration activities across frontier and offshore basins, particularly in the Andaman, Mahanadi and Kerala–Konkan regions. It is also undertaking extensive geological and geophysical studies in the Assam–Arakan, Rajasthan, Mahanadi and Andaman basins to identify additional hydrocarbon resources and strengthen its reserve base. The Company currently operates one of the largest exploration and production acreages in the country, with a presence across major sedimentary basins in India. 

The Company’s proposed offshore drilling programme comprises exploration and appraisal activities across key offshore basins. In the Andaman and Kerala–Konkan OALP Blocks, together with the Krishna–Godavari DSF Block, the Company is progressing seismic interpretation, appraisal and exploratory drilling activities. 

An additional 600 sq. km of 3D seismic data has been acquired around Sri Vijayapuram-2 and Sri Vijayapuram-3 in the Andaman region, with data processing currently underway. An appraisal well in the Andaman East Block, AN-OSHP-2018/1, is planned in Q3 of 2026-27. 

A stratigraphic well in the Mahanadi Basin is scheduled for April 2027 to assess the basin’s prospectivity. Exploratory drilling in the Mahanadi and Krishna– Godavari OALP Blocks is expected to follow the completion of seismic-data processing and the ongoing procurement of drillships and associated services. 

During FY2025–26, the Company established the presence of natural gas in the Andaman Basin and confirmed hydrocarbon presence in the North Bank area of the Brahmaputra under the OALP-I Block. The Company also commenced commercial natural gas production from the Bakhrittiba DSF-III Block in Rajasthan in June 2025. In the Baghewala DSF Block 

in Rajasthan, the Company achieved monetisation in record time, demonstrating the rapid commercialisation of discoveries under the Discovered Small Fields regime. 

# **Technology and Operational Excellence** 

Innovation and technology remain central to the Company’s growth strategy. The Company’s R&D Centre at Duliajan and the Centre of Excellence for Energy Studies in Guwahati support technological advancement across exploration, drilling, reservoir management, production optimisation, carbon management and digital transformation. 

The Company continues to collaborate with leading national and international academic institutions, research organisations and technology partners to accelerate innovation, strengthen technical capabilities and improve operational efficiency. 

# **Integrated Value-Chain Expansion** 

Following the acquisition of a 69.63% stake in NRL, the Company has transformed into a fully integrated energy company, with a presence across the upstream, midstream, downstream, petrochemical and city gas distribution value chains. 

The ongoing expansion of NRL’s refining capacity from 3 MMTPA to 9 MMTPA, together with associated petrochemical and infrastructure projects, is expected to strengthen the Company’s downstream presence and enhance its contribution to India’s energy security. 

During FY2025–26, NRL recorded its highest-ever crude receipt and throughput of 3.113 MMTPA since inception. The augmentation of the Numaligarh–Siliguri Product Pipeline increased its transportation capacity from 1.72 MMTPA to 5.5 MMTPA. The project was completed and inaugurated by the Hon’ble Prime Minister on 13<sup>th</sup> March 2026, generating cost savings of more than ` 110 crore through efficient project execution. The Company also achieved its highest-ever crude oil pipeline transportation volume of 7.453 MMT. 

NRL is also setting up a 360 KTPA polypropylene unit, expected to be commissioned in FY2027–28. The project is expected to enhance petrochemical integration and value addition while supporting the Company’s transformation into a diversified integrated energy company. 

153 



## **Energy Transition and Diversification** 

The Company is diversifying its energy portfolio to support India’s energy transition, with a target of increasing the contribution of non-hydrocarbon businesses to 12–14% by 2040. While continuing to invest in renewable energy, including solar and wind power, the Company is expanding into emerging areas such as green hydrogen, biotechnology, geothermal energy and Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage. These initiatives are intended to support sustainable growth and reduce carbon emissions. The Company has also entered the critical-minerals sector by securing mineral blocks in Arunachal Pradesh and Rajasthan. It is establishing strategic partnerships with domestic and international organisations to develop capabilities across the critical-minerals value chain and strengthen resource security for cleanenergy technologies. 

In the clean-fuels segment, the Company plans to establish 25 compressed biogas plants across India using municipal solid waste and agricultural residues as feedstock. Projects are currently under construction at Tinsukia and Bhubaneswar. Letters of Award have been issued for the Jorhat and Agartala projects, while the Cuttack and Sambalpur projects are at the tendering stage. The remaining projects are at various stages of implementation. 

Further strengthening the Company’s energy-transition portfolio, its material subsidiary, NRL, has commissioned a 50 KTPA second-generation bioethanol plant based on bamboo feedstock and is developing a 2.4 KTPA green hydrogen plant for refinery operations. 

# **3. Opportunities and Threats / Risks and Concerns** 

## **Opportunities** 

The Company is well positioned to capitalize on emerging opportunities arising from India’s evolving energy landscape and supportive policy environment. The Government of India’s continued focus on enhancing domestic hydrocarbon production through upcoming Open Acreage Licensing Policy (OALP) bid rounds, expansion of exploration acreage and opening of previously restricted areas is expected to create significant growth opportunities for exploration and production companies. The implementation of the new Petroleum and Natural Gas (PNG) Rules, effective from December 2025, marks a major reform in the upstream sector by simplifying approvals, enhancing operational flexibility, enabling integrated development of petroleum leases, improving ease of doing business and providing greater clarity and stability to investors. These reforms are expected to accelerate exploration activities, reduce project timelines and attract higher levels of investment into the sector. 

The Company’s extensive acreage portfolio, strong technical capabilities and strategy of partnering with national and international oil companies, technology providers and service companies place it in a favourable position to benefit from future OALP and DSF opportunities. The Company’s recent exploration successes in frontier basins such as Andaman and its continued focus on reserve accretion further strengthen its long-term growth prospects. 



154 

Simultaneously, India’s energy transition agenda presents substantial opportunities for business diversification. Government initiatives promoting renewable energy, biofuels, green hydrogen, Compressed Bio Gas (CBG) and sustainable mobility are creating new investment avenues across the energy value chain. Leveraging its integrated energy business model, the Company is expanding its presence in solar and wind energy, green hydrogen, biofuels, critical minerals, geothermal energy and Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage (CCUS). The Company has planned investments of approximately ` 20,000 crore by 2040 towards energy transition and net-zero initiatives through a dedicated wholly owned subsidiary viz. OGEL for alternate energy businesses. 

The adoption of advanced technologies, including artificial intelligence, data analytics, digital oilfield solutions, automation and advanced drilling techniques, is expected to further enhance operational efficiency, improve reservoir management and optimize production. Coupled with a strong focus on Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) practices, these initiatives will strengthen Company’s competitiveness and sustainability credentials. Supported by its legacy of technological innovation, diversified business portfolio and integrated energy presence, the Company is well positioned to drive future growth, contribute to India’s energy security and support the country’s long-term decarbonization & sustainability objectives.

# **4. Segment-Wise / Product Wise Performances** 

## **i. Crude Oil** 

During FY 2025–26, crude oil production stood at 3.450 MMT as against 3.458 MMT in the previous year, registering a marginal decline of 0.23%. Crude oil sales were 3.334 MMT, compared to 3.346 MMT in FY 2024– 25. Despite the natural decline in mature fields and an economic blockade in parts of Upper Assam, production was sustained through strategic initiatives including IOR/EOR, accelerated monetisation of new discoveries, production optimisation, advanced technologies, recovery of missed opportunities, infill drilling, monetisation of sick wells, Cyclic Steam Stimulation (CSS) in Rajasthan, and upgradation of surface facilities. Low Market Demand (LMD) for associated natural gas resulted in an opportunity loss of 0.057 MMT of crude oil production. 

The Company achieved a terminal crude oil production rate of 10,566 MTPD, the highest in the last 14 years, reflecting the success of sustained drilling, workover and production optimisation efforts. Overall crude oil production of 3.450 MMT represented 86% achievement against the MoU target of 4.034 MMT. 

Crude oil sales accounted for approximately 97% of total production. Sales from Assam & Arunachal Pradesh were 3.282 MMT against production of 3.387 MMT (97%), while Rajasthan recorded sales of 0.034 MMT against production of 0.044 MMT (including 250 MT of condensate), representing 77% of production. Average crude oil price realisation declined to USD 69.04/bbl from USD 78.09/bbl in the previous year. 

The production shortfall against the MoU target was primarily attributable to consequential production losses of 0.099 MMT due to economic blockade and other associated environmental constraints. Operation related losses amounted to 4,095 MT, attributable 

156 

to operational and maintenance-related activities associated with field operations. Further, the natural decline in wellhead production potential across mature producing fields, estimated at 1,516 MTPD, contributed to the overall production shortfall during FY 2025–26. Additionally, production losses of 9,999 MT were incurred due to Low Market Demand (LMD), comprising 296 MT from Company-operated areas and 9,703 MT representing Company’s share from Dirok JV. Despite these challenges, the Company maintained production momentum, which also enabled its material subsidiary NRL to achieve the highest refinery throughput since inception. 

- a. Carbonated Water Injection 

- b. Capturing, liquefaction, storage, transportation and pumping of CO2 – The Company has initiated a feasibility study for sequestration of the captured CO2 in saline aquifers in the deserts of Rajasthan 

- c. Rajasthan Field: 

FY 2025–26 was a landmark year for the Rajasthan Field (RF), which achieved its highest-ever crude oil production since inception of 43,773.41 MT, along with the highest-ever daily production rate of 1,202 BOPD. These achievements were driven by an intensified drilling campaign, optimisation of Cyclic Steam Stimulation (CSS) operations, introduction of barefoot completion, and innovative production enhancement initiatives. 

Under MISSION 4+, the Company aims to achieve sustained production of 4 MMT of crude oil and 5 BCM of natural gas through accelerated field development, intensified drilling and deployment of advanced technologies. Operational capabilities are being strengthened through augmentation of workover rigs, induction of VFD-enabled drilling rigs, enhancement of artificial lift systems and development of production infrastructure. The Company is also expanding Production Enhancement Contracts (PECs), deploying advanced production technologies, accelerating monetisation of low-performing wells, reassessing the Main Producing Areas (MPAs) using integrated 3D seismic interpretation, and progressing multiple EOR initiatives. These measures, supported by digitalisation, data-driven reservoir management and Government policy support, are expected to enhance long-term production and energy security. 

During the year, RF successfully drilled 12 wells (BGW041 to BGW-052) using barefoot completion, introduced for the first time in BGW-041. The wells demonstrated encouraging cold production rates of 15–30 BOPD and significantly higher production following CSS, establishing barefoot completion as a key development strategy. Improved drilling practices and efficient drill bit technologies also reduced drilling time, resulting in estimated savings of approximately ` 0.90 crore per well. 

RF completed 19 CSS cycles, the highest executed in a single year since commencement of thermal recovery operations. Deployment of an additional CSS unit improved operational flexibility and enabled successful CSS implementation in barefoot wells BGW-042, BGW043 and BGW-048. CSS and production optimisation initiatives contributed 10,768 MT of crude oil, accounting for 24.6% of the total annual production of 43,773 MT. 

Actions have been initiated for implementation of following projects, which are in different phases: 



157 



The record production was further supported by innovative production optimisation measures, including introduction of short-duration CSS cycles, in-house surfactant thermal stimulation without any additional capital investment, and prioritised selection of CSS candidate wells based on production potential and economic returns. In addition, deployment of liquid casing technology improved wellbore stability, reduced formation fluid losses and lowered chemical consumption costs by approximately 2%. 

# **Technology Induction and Innovation in RF** 

Rajasthan Field (RF) continued to strengthen its technological capabilities through the induction of advanced production and digital technologies. Fishbone Completion Technology, first implemented in Baghewala Well BGW-040, delivered an incremental production gain of approximately 70 BOPD, making it the highest producing well in the field at around 140 BOPD. Based on its success, five additional wells have been identified for Fishbone completion during FY 2027–28 and FY 2028–29. 

The Company also commissioned its first Real-Time Downhole Pressure-Temperature Monitoring System (RTMS) in BGW-035 during June 2025, enabling continuous reservoir monitoring and supporting improved CSS design, reservoir characterization and production optimization. 

Implementation of Multi-Stage Physio-Chemical (MPC) Technology has been planned in six wells (four in the Jodhpur Sandstone reservoir and two in the Upper Carbonate formation) from October 2026. The technology is expected to enhance reservoir connectivity and production, with the Jodhpur Sandstone wells anticipated to contribute approximately 40 BOPD, while establishing sustained production from the Upper Carbonate reservoir. 

RF has also adopted cluster J-bend well development to optimize infrastructure utilization, improve reservoir drainage and reduce environmental footprint, with estimated savings of approximately ` 0.60 crore per well. In line with its Net-Zero target by 2040, the Company is establishing a pilot Gas Sweetening Unit (GSU) and Carbon Capture & Storage (CCS) facility at the Dandewala Gas Processing Complex. Following completion of the pre-feasibility study in July 2025, a suitable CO2 injection well location has been identified and the tendering process for surface facilities and the injection well has been initiated. 

# **ii. Natural Gas** 

During FY 2025–26, the Company produced 3.186 BCM of natural gas against the MoU target of 3.889 BCM, achieving 81.93% of the target. Production comprised 2.863 BCM from Assam & Arunachal Pradesh, 0.255 BCM from Rajasthan Fields, and 0.068 BCM as the Company’s share from Dirok JV. Natural gas sales stood at 2.632 BCM, representing approximately 83% of production, including 2.243 BCM from Assam & Arunachal Pradesh and 0.250 BCM from Rajasthan, corresponding to 98% evacuation of Rajasthan production. 

However, total opportunity loss in natural gas production due to LMD (Low Market Demand) and low upliftment by major consumer is 0.221 BCM and opportunity loss due bandhs/blockades etc is 0.009 BCM which is not attributable to the Company. Moreover, opportunity loss due to lack of evacuation is 0.175 BCM. Revenue from natural gas increased to ` 5,636.72 crore from ` 5,514.09 crore in the previous year, while the weighted average gas price realization remained largely stable at US$ 6.64/ MMBTU compared to US$ 6.68/MMBTU in FY 2024–25. The shortfall against the MoU targets was primarily due to lower consumer offtake and inadequate evacuation infrastructure for connectivity to the National Gas Grid, limiting monetization of available gas potential. 

# **Rajasthan Field – Record Natural Gas Production** 

During FY 2025–26, Rajasthan Field (RF) achieved its highest-ever natural gas production since inception, producing 254.99 MMSCM, including 23.13 MMSCM from the DSF Contract Area, and achieving 81.73% of the annual target of 312 MMSCM. Gas sales also reached a record 250.40 MMSCM, while ensuring uninterrupted gas supply to RRVUNL through the GAIL pipeline network. 

A key milestone was the successful monetization of the Bakhritibba DSF-III Contract Area, with gas production commencing on 1 June 2025, making it one of the fastest monetization achievements under the DSF Round-III framework. Awarded to the Company in September 2022 with 100% Participating Interest, the project involved successful drilling and completion of three development wells (BGT-004, BGT-005 and BGT-006) within the stipulated development period ending 15 June 2026, qualifying the Company for early monetization incentives. The field is currently producing approximately 78,000 SCMD of natural gas, with plans to enhance production to 100,000 SCMD

## **North-East Gas Grid Connectivity: Unlocking Efficient Gas Evacuation and Market Access** 

Approval for the expansion of the North-East Gas Grid through the laying of a pipeline from Duliajan to Sectionalizing Valve Station-14 (SV-14) of the Guwahati– Numaligarh Pipeline was obtained in February, 2026. This strategic project will enhance the Company’s gas evacuation capacity, facilitate monetization of additional and stranded gas reserves, and support the growing demand from the industrial, commercial, City Gas Distribution (CGD) and power sectors. 

To strengthen its gas portfolio, the Company is accelerating exploration, development drilling, workover operations and production optimization across its key operational areas in Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, and other prospective basins. Simultaneously, investments are being made in critical gas infrastructure, including Non-Associated Gas (NAG) wells, gas gathering stations, compression facilities, pipeline networks, and gas processing and evacuation systems. These initiatives are expected to enhance production, improve operational efficiency, reduce routine gas flaring, and contribute to India’s energy security and clean energy transition. 

These projects are expected to give substantial gain in natural gas production potential of the Company upon completion: 

- (a) A Group Gathering Station at East Khagorijan, along with pipeline infrastructure 

- (b) Gas Gathering Station at Baghjan 

- (c) Revamping of old installations 

- (d) Group Gathering Station at Lakwagaon 

RF continued its dedicated efforts to ensure efficient production operations and uninterrupted supply of natural gas to RRVUNL in accordance with the GSA through the pipeline network of GAIL (India) Limited, thereby supporting the energy requirements of the State of Rajasthan and contributing significantly to the overall annual performance of the Company. 

## **iii. Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG)** 

During FY 2025–26, the LPG Recovery Plant achieved an availability of 99.89%, while butane recovery efficiency stood at 98.59%, exceeding the design specification of 

98%. The plant processed an average of 1.83 MMSCMD (66.15 MMSCFD) of gas with an average butane content of 1.01% (v/v) and operated for 338 days, producing 30,906 MT of LPG. In addition, 20,925 MT of condensate was recovered as a by-product and added to the Company’s crude oil production. The LPG Filling Plant operated for 276 days, dispatching the entire LPG production to IOCL in bulk tankers. Revenue from LPG sales stood at ` 166.39 crore, while condensate realization was ` 25.56 crore as against ` 30.45 crore in the previous year. 

## **iv. Pipeline Operations** 

During FY 2025–26, the Company achieved its highestever crude oil transportation of 7.453 MMT, surpassing 7.145 MMT in the previous year. The Digboi–Naharkatia– Bongaigaon sector transported 3.282 MMT of the Company’s crude oil, 1.040 MMT for ONGC and 0.032 MMT from JVC, while the Barauni–Bongaigaon– Guwahati sector transported a record 3.098 MMT of imported crude oil. The Numaligarh–Siliguri Product Pipeline (NSPL) transported 1.724 MMT of petroleum products. Transportation revenue increased to ` 936.20 crore (including ` 263.11 crore arrear recovery arising from tariff revision, excluding ` 6.74 crore from telecom business) compared to ` 572.23 crore in the previous year (excluding ` 9.28 crore from telecom business). 

The Company operates 1,243 km of crude oil pipelines and a 654 km product pipeline. During the year, pipeline reliability and safety were strengthened through infrastructure modernization, while Phase-II of the trunk pipeline rehabilitation project covering the remaining ~700 km was initiated in December 2024. 

The NSPL Capacity Augmentation Project, increasing pipeline capacity from 1.72 MMTPA to 5.5 MMTPA to support NRL’s expansion from 3 MMTPA to 9 MMTPA, was dedicated to the nation by the Hon’ble Prime Minister of India on 13 March 2026. The project incorporates advanced automation and leak detection technologies, is expected to be completed at around ` 750 crore against the approved cost of ` 860 crore, and achieved over 4 million LTA-free man-hours during execution. 

# **5. Financial Performance** 

During the FY 2025-26, the Company has earned total revenue of ` 24,038.58 crore as against ` 23,987.07 crore in the previous year. Revenue remained broadly stable during the year as the impact of lower crude oil price realizations was largely offset by higher transportation income, higher dividend and stable natural gas revenues. 

159 



The Net profit margin of the Company for FY 2025-26 was 20.87%. The Profit Before Tax (PBT) in the FY 202526 was ` 5,419.86 crore against PBT of ` 7,850.95 crore in the previous year. The decline in Profit Before Tax during FY 2025–26 was primarily attributable to lower crude oil price realizations, higher exploratory well write-offs and provisions, increased contract expenditure arising from expanded exploration and seismic activities and 

increased foreign exchange losses on revaluation of foreign currency borrowings. These were partially offset by lower statutory levies following the withdrawal of the Special Additional Excise Duty (SAED). 

The Company has registered Profit After Tax (PAT) at ` 4,455.34 crore during FY 2025-26 as against ` 6,114.19 crore in the previous year.

# **6. Internal Control System** 

Internal Audit in the Company is an independent corporate reporting function that provides objective 

assurance on the adequacy and effectiveness of the Company’s internal control system, risk management framework, and governance processes. It assesses whether these mechanisms are appropriately designed, effectively implemented and functioning as intended to safeguard assets, ensure compliance with applicable laws and policies and aligned with the Company’s strategic and operational objectives. 

The Audit & Ethics Committee, under the overall supervision of the Board of Directors, exercises oversight of the Internal Audit function. The Committee periodically reviews audit plans, key findings and management responses and monitors the timely implementation of corrective actions, thereby ensuring the strengthening of internal controls and safeguarding of stakeholders’ interests. 

The Company follows a structured risk-based internal audit approach covering the entire Audit Universe, including all business processes, functions and operations. The annual audit plan is developed through a systematic risk assessment to prioritize high-risk and critical areas. A digitalized system of audit reporting enhances audit execution, tracking of observations and monitoring of corrective actions. The use of technology and analytics strengthens internal controls, improves transparency and supports proactive risk management across the organization.

# **7. Human Resource** 

Your Company’s human capital remains a critical enabler of operational resilience, business growth, and long-term value creation. In FY 2025–26, the Company continued to strengthen workforce capabilities, leadership depth, employee engagement, and digital readiness in alignment with its strategic priorities and the evolving energy landscape. The Company’s people strategy is anchored on creating a future-ready workforce capable of supporting operational excellence, innovation, safety, and sustainable growth. 

## **Workforce Stability, Talent Renewal & Diversity** 

The Company maintained a stable workforce with very low voluntary attrition, reflecting strong employee commitment and organisational stability. Strategic recruitment and internal talent development continued to support succession requirements and emerging business opportunities. Alongside workforce renewal efforts, the Company remained committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion through inclusive hiring, adherence to Government reservation policies, and initiatives aimed at improving representation across workforce segments. Increased participation of women in executive recruitment reflects continued progress toward building a more balanced and diverse organisation. 

## **Capability Building & Leadership Development** 

Capability development continues to be a strategic priority for the Company as the Company prepares for future business challenges and opportunities. During the year, learning initiatives were delivered through a blended ecosystem comprising classroom programmes, digital learning platforms, and competency-based interventions. A significant milestone was achieved through the Company’s pioneering integration with the iGOT Karmayogi platform, strengthening access to learning and knowledge resources. 

The Company also strengthened its leadership pipeline through structured initiatives such as Aarohan, the Company’s flagship leadership development journey, DAKSH, the Government of India’s leadership programme for CPSE executives, and BizHR, aimed at enhancing the business and strategic capabilities of HR professionals. These interventions contribute towards succession readiness, leadership bench strength, and organisational agility in an increasingly dynamic business environment. 

## **Employee Engagement, Well-being & Workplace Culture** 

The Company continued to foster a culture of engagement, recognition, collaboration, and employee well-being. Leadership outreach initiatives, employee recognition programmes, wellness interventions, sports and team-building activities, and continuous communication platforms helped strengthen workforce morale and organisational commitment. The Company also maintained a strong focus on workplace dignity, safety, and inclusiveness through established grievance redressal and awareness mechanisms, reinforcing a culture of mutual respect and accountability. 

## **Digital HR Transformation** 

The Company accelerated its digital HR transformation agenda with a focus on enhancing service delivery, transparency, and data-driven decision-making. Ongoing initiatives in process automation, employee self-service systems, learning analytics, workforce management, and digital governance are improving employee experience while enabling HR to play a more strategic role in organisational planning and performance management. These initiatives are expected to further strengthen operational efficiency and organisational responsiveness in the years ahead. 

## **Linkage to Sustainability & Business Strategy** 

Human capital remains central to the Company’s sustainability and growth agenda. The Company’s people strategy supports operational excellence, safety performance, energy transition preparedness, and organisational resilience. Continuous investment in capability enhancement, leadership development, and workforce reskilling is helping prepare employees for emerging opportunities across conventional and new energy domains, including renewables, compressed biogas, critical minerals, and other evolving business areas. The Company’s leadership continues to monitor human capital indicators as part of its broader focus on sustainable value creation and ESG performance. 

## **Industrial Relations & Social Partnership** 

The Company continued to maintain a harmonious industrial relations climate through proactive engagement with employee unions and executive associations. Constructive dialogue, collaborative problem-solving, and timely grievance resolution contributed to smooth operations and strengthened trust

between management and employees. The Company’s strong industrial relations framework continues to support productivity, project implementation, and organisational stability.

# **11. Discovery of Oil and Gas** 

Your Company has made 02 (two) discoveries during FY 2025-26,  the details are as follows: 

**Well East Borpothar-1:** Oil discovery was made in Borhapjan PML in Assam in the exploratory well East Borpathar-1 (Loc .BHD). The well was drilled upto 4600 m and a total of 07 prospective zones were encountered in the well, out of which the 4380-m Lk+Th Sand was tested and the well produced crude oil @ 80 KLPD (API26.3°, PP-39°C) with water @ 4 KLPD (Salinity-300 ppm, HCO3-4575 ppm) through 5 mm bean. The discovery is the result of Company’s continued Near Field exploration pursuit in its nomination acreages in proven petroliferous basins. 

**Well Namrup-Borhat-2:** Oil discovery was made in the exploratory well Namrup Borhat-2 (Loc. NOAB) in OALP-I Block AA-ONHP-2017/20 in Assam. The well was spudded on 09.07.2024 and drilled down to depth of 4403 m targeting the Oligocene play. The 4333-m Barail sand was tested and the well produced crude oil @13 klpd (API-31.1° 

165 



& PP-33°C). The appraisal plan includes the extended testing of the oil-bearing sand interval along with testing of other prospective sands encountered in the well. It is also planned to drill one more exploratory Loc. NOAC for probing the Eocene and Barail plays in the Block. 

In a significant breakthrough, the Company also established presence of gas in exploratory well Vijaya Puram-2 (Loc. OAEA) in OALP-II Block AN-OSHP-2018/1 in Andaman East shallow offshore. The well was spudded on 23.05.2025 and drilled upto 2961 m in Eocene play. On testing the 2212-m Eocene sand, the well recorded an immediate pressure build-up of 1000 psi while flowing formation water along with intermittent gas. Gas compositional analysis indicated CH4 concentration of 87% (Net Calorific Value-7217 Kcal/SCM, Gross Calorific Value-8013 Kcal/SCM). The testing results mark only as a technical success at this stage with no commercial flow established in the well. Around 600 SQKM of highresolution 3D seismic data is planned to be acquired in the Block to refine the next phase of exploration in the area.

Diversification into Critical Minerals Domain: Critical minerals present a significant opportunity to support the global energy transition and India’s commitment to achieving net-zero emissions by 2070. These minerals are indispensable for clean energy technologies, including solar panels, wind turbines, semiconductors, electric vehicles and advanced energy storage systems. In line with this strategic vision, the Company has actively participated in Tranche-IV and Tranche-V critical mineral auctions conducted by the Ministry of Mines and has emerged as the Preferred Bidder for two mineral blocks: the Phop Graphite & Vanadium Block in Arunachal Pradesh and the Jorkian–Satipura–Khunja Potash & Halite Block in Rajasthan. 

For the Phop Block, the Company completed all preexploration activities, secured the Composite Licence in December 2025 and commenced the exploration phase, with detailed exploration to be undertaken in collaboration with Mineral Exploration and Consultancy Limited (MECL). For the Jorkian Block, pre-exploration activities are underway and the Scheme of Prospecting has been submitted for regulatory approval. Detailed exploration is planned to follow the grant of the Composite Licence. 

166 

To strengthen its critical minerals portfolio, the Company has established strategic partnerships with leading domestic organizations, including GSI, IREL, Hindustan Copper, MECL, CSIR laboratories, IITs and RSMML, while internationally collaborating with KABIL, International Resources Holding, Africa Finance Corporation and YPF to pursue overseas exploration, resource development and value-chain opportunities 

**CCUS and Geothermal:** The Company is actively advancing low-carbon technologies through initiatives in CCUS, CCS and geothermal energy. A feasibility study for permanent CORajasthan, has identified a suitable saline aquifer, with 2 storage in the Jaisalmer Basin, plans for pilot-scale injection through two injection wells and one monitoring well, supported by ongoing surface facility and drilling preparations. In Assam, Carbonated Water Injection (CWI) has been planned as an Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR) scheme in the Dikom field. Additional in the Makum–North Hapjan and Kathaloni oilfields studies are underway to evaluate CO2-EOR potential through collaborations with technical partners, including Texas A&M Engineering Experiment Station (USA). The Company is also pursuing membrane-based CO2 separation, compression, transportation and permanent subsurface storage, alongside laboratory research on CO2 mineralization in Deccan Trap basalts. Separately, a CCS pilot project has been initiated in Rajasthan. 

The Company is advancing its geothermal energy initiatives through strategic collaborations with Iceland GeoSurvey, the Government of Himachal Pradesh, and the Geological Survey of India for geothermal exploration. Feasibility studies are currently underway in Arunachal Pradesh, in association with CES & HS, to assess the geothermal potential of hot springs. Additionally, a consultancy study has been initiated to evaluate the feasibility of repurposing abandoned oil and gas wells in the Upper Assam Basin for geothermal energy development. 

**CBG:** In alignment with the GOBARdhan Scheme and under the guidance of the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas (MoP&NG), the Company is actively developing 25 CBG plants across India using diverse feedstocks, including Municipal Solid Waste (MSW), agricultural residues and other organic biomass. The initiative is a key component of the Company’s clean energy and circular economy strategy, aimed at promoting sustainable waste management while enhancing the domestic production of green fuels. 

Construction activities are currently in progress for the CBG plants at Tinsukia, Bhubaneswar, Jorhat and Agartala. The Tinsukia and Bhubaneswar projects are 

targeted for commissioning by March 2027, while the Jorhat and Agartala plants are scheduled for completion by March 2028. The Company has also secured land for nine additional project locations, creating a strong pipeline for future capacity expansion. EPC-cumOperation & Maintenance (O&M) tenders have been floated for the Cuttack and Sambalpur projects, while Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) have been completed for 13 additional locations. The remaining projects are at various stages of planning, tendering and implementation. 

To accelerate the rollout of its bio-energy programme, the Company has obtained approval from the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) for the formation of Joint Venture Companies (JVCs) with GPS Renewables Pvt. Ltd. and Hindustan Waste Treatment Pvt. Ltd. (HWTPL). The Joint Venture Agreement (JVA) with HWTPL has already been executed and the process for incorporation of the Joint Venture Company is currently underway, providing a strong institutional framework for expanding the Company’s CBG portfolio across the country. 

**Renewable Energy:** As part of its energy transition strategy, the Company is steadily expanding its renewable energy portfolio with a long-term target of deploying 5–5.5 GW of renewable energy capacity by 2040, encompassing solar, wind, green hydrogen and other sustainable energy initiatives. 

As on 31<sup>st</sup> March 2026, total installed capacity of the Company in respect of renewable energy stands at 188.10 MW (excluding projects for captive utilization), comprising of 174.10 MW of wind energy projects and 14 MW of solar energy projects. In addition, solar plants of 2261 kWp are being used for captive utilization in different spheres of the Company. 

The 25 MW solar power project at Namrup, Assam,  by APGCL OIL Green Power Limited (AOGPL), a JV Company with Assam Power Generation Corporation Limited (APGCL) is currently under construction and is targeted for commissioning by March 2027. 

In addition, the Company has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Government of Rajasthan to invest approximately ` 4,700 crore in the development of 1,000 MW of solar and 200 MW of wind power capacity by 2030. The proposal for formation of the Joint Venture Company has been submitted to the DIPAM for concurrence. Green Hydrogen: The Company is actively advancing green hydrogen technologies in alignment with the National Green Hydrogen Mission. 

167 



The Company has commissioned a 30 kg/day Anion Exchange Membrane (AEM) electrolyser-based pilot plant at Jorhat, Assam, which has received approval from the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) for blending up to 2% green hydrogen with natural gas, and blending operations are currently underway. In collaboration with Himachal Pradesh Power Corporation Limited (HPPCL), the Company is also constructing a 1 MW alkaline electrolyser-based Green Hydrogen plant at Nalagarh, Himachal Pradesh. Additionally, the Company is planning to establish a 10 MW Green Hydrogen plant at Duliajan, Assam. 

The Company’s subsidiary, NRL, is also implementing a 300 kg/hr (2.4 KTPA) Green Hydrogen plant at Numaligarh through M/s Greenco ZeroC, India, on an EPC basis. The project will replace approximately 5% of the refinery’s existing grey hydrogen consumption, reducing CO2 emissions by about 24,000 tonnes annually. NRL is also planning to float a tender for setting up a 5 KTPA Green Hydrogen plant on a Build, Own and Operate (BOO) basis under the SIGHT Scheme (Mode-2B) of the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) to further enhance the use of green hydrogen in refinery operations 

**Strategic Refining and Midstream Partnerships:** The Company and BPCL have entered into a collaborative framework to explore the Company’s participation in the proposed integrated Greenfield refinery and petrochemical complex at Ramayapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, with an estimated investment of approximately ` 1 lakh crore. Under the framework, the two companies will evaluate the feasibility for acquiring a minority equity stake in the proposed joint venture. 

The proposed complex is envisaged with a refining capacity of 9–12 MMTPA, integrated with a 1.5 MMTPA ethylene cracker unit and is targeted for commercial commissioning during FY 2030. 

Separately, OIL, NRL and BPCL have signed a tripartite MoU to facilitate efficient evacuation of petroleum products following NRL’s capacity expansion from 3 MMTPA to 9 MMTPA. As part of this collaboration, the three companies will jointly examine the development of a cross-country petroleum product pipeline from Siliguri to Mughalsarai via Muzaffarpur, along with augmentation of depot infrastructure, involving an estimated investment of approximately ` 3,500 crore. 

# **14. Future Outlook:** 

Global oil markets enter FY2025–26 against a backdrop of improving stability following a period of elevated geopolitical and market uncertainty. The disruptions witnessed during calendar year 2025 and early 2026, 

arising from the conflict in West Asia and constraints on transit through the Strait of Hormuz, have to the extent subsided, supporting a gradual normalisation of supply chains and market sentiment. Nevertheless, the outlook remains shaped by geopolitical developments, global economic growth, supply management by major producing nations and the pace of the energy transition, all of which are expected to influence commodity prices and investment decisions. 

The IEA reported Hormuz flows recovering from a May 2026 low of 9.6 million barrels per day to roughly 12 million barrels per day by mid-June. Even so, the IEA and EIA still project global oil demand to contract by close to 1.0–1.2 million barrels per day for 2026, though OPEC’s outlook remains materially more bullish, emphasizing the unusual degree of forecaster variation this year. The outlook inflects sharply into 2027, where IEA, EIA and OPEC forecasts converge closely on demand growth of approximately 2.0 million barrels per day as trade flows normalise. For an upstream-anchored company such as OIL, this shift from a supply-constrained, price-volatile 2026 to a better-supplied, demand-recovering 2027 also reinforces the case for continued capital discipline, reserve replacement and cost competitiveness. 

India remains the principal bright spot within this global picture. The Indian economy is projected to grow at 6.5–6.6% in FY2026–27, with the country’s oil demand estimated at close to 5.99 million barrels per day in 2026, keeping India among the fastest-growing large oil and gas markets globally even as import dependence already close to 90%, continues to strengthen the case for domestic upstream investment. Government policy leans firmly in this direction: the 10<sup>th</sup> OALP bidding round, launched in February 2026, is the largest ever by acreage offered, spanning over 190,000 sq. km across 25 blocks, while the Union Budget for FY2025–26 allocated further capital toward Phase II of India’s Strategic Petroleum Reserve programme. Domestic natural gas demand is expected to grow faster still, supported by City Gas Distribution expansion, new fertiliser and petrochemical offtake, and continued build-out of national gas-grid infrastructure, aligned with the Company’s own NorthEast Gas Grid and Duliajan Feeder Line investments. 

The approval of the Samudra Manthan, National Offshore Exploration Scheme marks a defining inflection point for India’s upstream sector, signalling the transition from policy reforms to mission-mode execution. The Mission seeks to unlock India’s vast offshore hydrocarbon potential while significantly reducing exploration risk. For the Company, with its expanding presence in frontier offshore basins, the initiative provides a strong policy 

168 

and technological foundation to accelerate exploration, strengthen domestic hydrocarbon production and contribute meaningfully to India’s long-term energy security. 

Within this operating environment, the Company’s outlook for FY2026–27 is anchored in five strategic priorities, each carrying a demonstrated FY2025–26 track record forward: 

# **Strengthening Core E&P Operations** 

The Company’s future growth will continue to be anchored in strengthening its core exploration and production business through sustained reserve addition, accelerated resource monetisation and expansion into frontier exploration basins. The Government of India’s approval of the Samudra Manthan – National Offshore Exploration Scheme, with a Phase-I outlay of approximately ` 84,084 crore, marks a transformative step in unlocking the country’s offshore hydrocarbon potential. By promoting advanced geoscientific data acquisition, deepwater exploration, shared offshore infrastructure and cutting-edge technologies, the Mission is expected to significantly enhance India’s upstream exploration ecosystem and strengthen longterm energy security. 

Aligned with this national vision, the Company is strategically strengthening its presence across frontier offshore basins, including the Andaman, Mahanadi and Krishna-Godavari basins, while continuing to maximise value from its onshore portfolio through technologydriven exploration, improved recovery and operational excellence. 

Further to support this, the company is expanding its drilling and well intervention fleet of 28 operational rigs currently in service, four additional rigs are being procured taking the fleet to 32 rigs by the end of FY 2027-28. In parallel, five additional work-over rigs are being inducted adding to the existing fleet of 33, to support accelerated well delivery and field development. Going forward, the Company will leverage advanced subsurface analytics and collaborative partnerships to enhance exploration success, expand its resource base and create sustainable long-term value for stakeholders. 

# **Reserve Accretion and Frontier Exploration** 

The Company will continue to expand its domestic hydrocarbon resource base through near-field exploration, appraisal of existing discoveries, frontier-area exploration and improved subsurface understanding. The 2P Reserve Replacement Ratio, which improved to 1.02 in FY2025–26, is targeted to be 

sustained at or above unity; as of 31 March 2026, total 2P reserves stood at 68.68 MMT of crude oil and 50.58 BCM of natural gas with remaining recoverable gas 139.68 BCM. A drilling programme of approximately 78 wells is planned across the North-East Region during FY2026– 27 to build on this base. 

The Assam Shelf Basin  the Company’s Main Producing Area and a prolific onshore basin with considerable Yet-To-Find potential  remains the anchor of this effort, with acreage consolidation continuing under the Open Acreage Licensing Policy regime alongside exploration in the geologically prospective but geographically challenging North Bank of the Brahmaputra and the Fold Belt areas. Offshore, the Andaman campaign has established hydrocarbon presence in the Sri Vijaya Puram-2 and -3 wells, with a further 600 sq. km of acquired 3D seismic data under processing to guide future appraisal, while drilling continues at one location each in the Krishna–Godavari Shallow Water DSF contract area and the Kerala–Konkan Block. The Company has also submitted bids for select blocks under the Special CBM Bid Rounds 2025 and 2026, with evaluation by the Directorate General of Hydrocarbons in progress. 

# **Technology and Operational Excellence** 

Technology and digital innovation will remain central to recovery, drilling efficiency and reservoir management. Field trials of Liquid Casing Technology for wellbore stability, alongside flow-assurance studies covering lowtemperature demulsifiers and acidization formulations, are supporting uninterrupted reservoir-to-refinery hydrocarbon movement. 

The Company’s deployed technology base spanning Plunger-Assisted Gas Lift, Single-String Multi-Zone Completion, Microbial Enhanced Oil Recovery, Propellant Stimulation, an AI-enabled Well Portfolio Optimizer, Fishbone Drilling and Intelligent Well Completion Systems, among others — is being extended through the phased rollout of Real-Time Production Monitoring and Analysis. 

These initiatives are complemented by a strong ecosystem of strategic technology partnerships and collaborative research. The Company’s Technical Services Agreement (TSA) with TotalEnergies continues to strengthen capabilities in deepwater exploration through advanced seismic interpretation, prospect evaluation and well design. In parallel, the Company is leveraging the MC² collaborative platform, together with partnerships with the leading Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), to accelerate research and 

169 



technology development in optimization of artificial lift & cyclic steam stimulation, Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage (CCUS), geothermal energy and critical minerals. These collaborations are expected to de-risk future investments and accelerate technology adoption. 

To build a future-ready enterprise, the Company has launched DRIVE 2.0, a comprehensive digital transformation programme comprising 10 AI and Generative AI-enabled initiatives spanning the entire hydrocarbon value chain. The programme focuses on creating digital oilfields, intelligent well planning, predictive asset maintenance, digital twins, smart procurement, AI-enabled project monitoring, video analytics for safety, digital workforce management and an integrated Command & Control Centre. Together, these initiatives are aimed at improving production efficiency, reducing operational costs, strengthening asset reliability, enhancing workplace safety and enabling faster data-driven decision-making. 

As part of the renewed OIL–CSIR strategic collaboration, the Company signed two Project Specific Agreements with CSIR-NEERI to deploy research-driven, sustainable waste management solutions at Duliajan. The first project will establish an advanced Faecal Sludge and Septage Management (FSSM) system using NEERI’s Mechanical Dewatering and Drying System (MDDS) technology for scientific treatment and conversion of sludge into value-added manure. The second project focuses on scientific characterisation, resource recovery and valorisation of drilling waste, aimed at developing scalable technologies to convert solid/semisolid drilling waste into environmentally compliant, value-added products, thereby promoting circular economy principles and reducing environmental liabilities. 

Your Company and IFP Energies Nouvelles (IFPEN), France, signed a Master Agreement at IFPEN Headquarters in Paris. The Master Agreement establishes a long-term framework for collaboration in advanced subsurface characterization, reservoir modelling, enhanced oil recovery (EOR), digitalization and artificial intelligence, carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS), decarbonization, renewable energy, biofuels, energy storage and circular economy solutions.  The collaboration will also focus on evaluating the potential for underground natural gas storage in depleted oil and gas reservoirs and advancing natural hydrogen exploration through identifying   favourable geological settings within India’s sedimentary Basins. 

The collaboration would also promote joint research, technology development, innovation and capacity 

building through Indo-French initiatives such as CEFIPRA and    MC² + an initiative of the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, Government of India, accelerating the Company’s technology-driven growth while advancing India’s energy security and energy transition goals. 

MOU signed between the Petroleum Technology Research Centre (PTRC), a not-for-profit energy research company of the Province of Saskatchewan of Canada and the Company in the fields of CO2 Capture, Utilization and Storage (CCUS), Geothermal, development of Clean Energy Technologies and research interests with mc2+ for startups, a platform created under the aegis of Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, Government of India, 

# **Integrated Value-Chain Expansion** 

The Company will continue to build out its integrated energy value chain through gas evacuation infrastructure, crude transportation and downstream integration. Expansion of the North-East Gas Grid and associated gathering infrastructure is expected to monetise stranded and incremental gas volumes and widen access to industrial, commercial and City Gas Distribution markets, while the ongoing expansion of Numaligarh Refinery Limited’s capacity from 3 to 9 MMTPA together with associated pipeline and petrochemical projects will materially strengthen the Company’s downstream presence. The recently completed augmentation of the Numaligarh–Siliguri Product Pipeline to 5.5 MMTPA will support evacuation of the additional product volumes this expansion brings, and further midstream opportunities with strategic partners continue to be evaluated. 

# **Energy Transition and Diversification** 

Alongside strengthening its core hydrocarbon business, the Company will continue to diversify its portfolio into low-carbon and emerging energy businesses, including renewable energy, green hydrogen, compressed biogas (CBG), Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage (CCUS), geothermal energy and critical minerals. This measured diversification reflects the Company’s strategy of building complementary growth engines that leverage its core technical capabilities while supporting India’s evolving energy transition. Through continued project development, strategic partnerships, technology collaborations and investments across its subsidiaries and joint ventures, the Company aims to create a resilient and future-ready energy portfolio that broadens revenue streams, enhance long-term competitiveness and reinforce its position as a leading integrated energy company.

# **ANNUAL REPORT ON CSR ACTIVITIES 2025-26** 

## **1. Brief outline of the CSR & SD Policy of the Company** 

Oil India Limited (OIL) continues to uphold its commitment to being a responsible corporate citizen by integrating social, environmental, and economic priorities into its business philosophy. During FY 2025– 26, the Company’s CSR initiatives were strategically aligned with national developmental priorities and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Through a community-centric approach, OIL implemented impactful interventions across education, healthcare, livelihood, skill development, and infrastructure, ensuring sustainable and inclusive growth in its areas of operation. 

The Company’s CSR & SD Policy provides a structured framework for planning, implementing, and monitoring initiatives, supporting informed decision-making and the development of actionable annual plans. The Company’s CSR philosophy is rooted in its vision of being a Responsible Corporate Citizen. At Oil India Limited (OIL), Corporate Social Responsibility is not merely a statutory mandate instead it is a deeply embedded philosophy that reflects its commitment to inclusive growth and responsible nation-building. The Company continuously strives to harmonize economic progress with social equity and environmental stewardship, ensuring that its growth story meaningfully uplifts the communities it serves. 

## **Major CSR activities of the Company in FY 2025-26** 

### **a) Healthcare, Nutrition & Sanitation** 

In the healthcare domain, the Company adopted a holistic and community-driven approach toward improving health outcomes. **‘OIL Arogya’** addressed maternal and child healthcare, nutrition, and sanitation through health camps, awareness programs, and distribution of essential kits. To ensure last-mile healthcare delivery, **‘OIL Sparsha’** conducted extensive mobile medical camps, reaching remote populations with free consultation and medicines. 

Addressing menstrual health and hygiene, ‘ **OIL Shakti’** established community-based sanitary napkin production units managed by local women, while also creating awareness to break social stigma. **‘OIL Asha’** extended compassionate care by providing nutritional 

and psychological support to children undergoing cancer treatment, thereby strengthening survival outcomes and family resilience. 

**OIL Nursing School** at Duliajan offers a three-year Diploma in General Nursing and Midwifery (GNM), aimed at developing skilled healthcare professionals while empowering women. Recognized by national and state councils, the programme includes a one-year postqualification clinical training at OIL Hospital. 

The Company also contributed significantly to strengthening healthcare infrastructure through the organization of medical camps and eye surgery initiatives, provision of ambulance services, and support to hospitals, alongside the development of new patientcare facilities. These interventions have enhanced access to quality healthcare, particularly in remote and underserved areas. In parallel, the Company actively supported the Swachh Bharat Mission by promoting sanitation, hygiene awareness, and environmental cleanliness through community engagement initiatives. 

Further extending its commitment to community wellbeing, the Company undertook several projects aimed at improving quality of life and basic amenities. These included the installation of open gyms to promote health and fitness, deployment of solar street lighting to enhance safety and sustainability, construction of dedicated school toilets for girls to support education and dignity, and installation of RO water purification plants to ensure access to safe drinking water across various locations. 

### **Key impact areas:** 

- **OIL Arogya:** Improved maternal, child and community health across 30 villages, benefiting nearly 40,875 people. The initiative covered 4,500+ beneficiaries through health camps, reached 5,000+ people via community awareness programmes, distributed 4,500 hygiene kits, 360+ baby kits, and 1,500 nutrition kits, facilitated 1,500+ immunisations, implemented WASH-UNICEF initiatives benefiting 3,600+ people, supported 5,400+ schoolgirls through the School Adoption Programme, and established 15 Healthcare-Based Rural Social Enterprise Units along with 30+ model community nutrition gardens. 

- **OIL Sparsha:** Conducted 2,304 mobile health camps benefiting 1,16,476 patients

# **Summary of the Impact Assessment Report** 

Oil India Limited (OIL) continues to leverage Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) as a strategic instrument for creating sustainable and inclusive development. During FY 2025–26, the Company undertook a third-party impact assessment of 24 eligible CSR projects, in compliance with Companies (Corporate Social Responsibility Policy) Amendment Rules, 2021. The assessment, conducted using the OECD-DAC evaluation framework and Social Return on Investment (SRoI) methodology, covered projects across education, healthcare, skill development, sustainable livelihoods, women empowerment and community infrastructure. Collectively, these initiatives impacted over 1.96 lakh beneficiaries across multiple states. 

The findings reaffirm that OIL’s CSR initiatives have delivered measurable improvements in access to quality education, healthcare, livelihood opportunities and community infrastructure, while strengthening human capital, institutional capacities and community resilience. The assessment also highlighted lasting developmental outcomes through the creation of durable community assets, enhanced service delivery systems and meaningful interventions in Aspirational Districts. The SRoI analysis estimated that against a cumulative investment of ` 88.67 crore, the assessed projects generated a present social value of ` 385.73 crore, resulting in an overall SRoI of 4.35. This signifies that every ` 1 invested by OIL generated an estimated ` 4.35 of social value for beneficiaries, communities and institutions. The impact assessment underscores the effectiveness of OIL’s CSR approach in delivering measurable, sustainable and inclusive outcomes, reaffirming the Company’s commitment to responsible business practices and its continued contribution to India’s socio-economic development. 

The detailed impact assessment report (FY 2024-25) is available on the link: <u>https://www.oil-india.com/ fles/2026-08/OIL_CSR_Impact_Assessment_Final_Report_29_07_26.pdf</u>

# **REPORT ON CORPORATE GOVERNANCE** 

## **1. COMPANY’S PHILOSOPHY ON CORPORATE GOVERNANCE** 

Corporate Governance is a framework of principles, processes and practices that governs corporate conduct. At the core, the elements include independence, transparency, accountability, responsibility, compliance, ethics, values and trust. These elements enable an organization to operate efficiently, ethically and responsibly, while promoting long-term value creation for all its stakeholders. 

The Company believes that Corporate Governance is fundamental to building and sustaining stakeholder trust. Our governance system is intended to set high standards of ethical and responsible conduct of the Company’s business to maximise value for all stakeholders including shareholders, customers, employees, contractors, vendors and society at large. It aims to strengthen the relationship of trust between Company & its stakeholders and helps to achieve Company’s goals and objectives. It is ensured that all stakeholders get their fair share in its earnings & assets and all material information is disclosed. The Company is committed to operate its businesses in legal, ethical and transparent manner. 

Corporate Governance reflects our value system. Through effective corporate governance, Board seeks to embed and sustain a culture that will enable Company to fulfil its purpose and achieve its long-term strategic objectives, by building durable partnerships 

and upholding its core values of Integrity & Ethics, excellence and Technology & Innovation. 

## **2. BOARD OF DIRECTORS** 

### **2.1  Composition** 

The Board of the Company comprises of Functional Directors [including Chairman and Managing Director (CMD)], Nominee Directors from the Administrative Ministry i.e. Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas (MoP&NG) and the Independent Directors. The Independent Directors appointed on the Board of the Company are eminent personalities drawn from fields like Management, Law, Finance, Administration etc. having wide experience in their respective fields. As on 31.03.2026, the Board of the Company comprised of 8 (Eight) Directors which includes 5 (Five) Functional Directors [including CMD], 2 (Two) Government Nominee Directors and 1 (One) Independent Director. 

Upon induction on the Board of the Company, the Directors are familiarized with profile of the Company, its business, industry scenario, operations, organizational structure, statutory & regulatory responsibilities through familiarization programme which is also available on the Company’s website.

# **Remuneration** 

The Pay and allowances for Board Level and below Board Level employees are decided on the basis of Guidelines issued by Department of Public Enterprises (DPE) and the profitability of the Company. The proposal for pay revision is sent to Administrative Ministry for issuance of Presidential Directives in this regard after it has been recommended by Nomination & Remuneration Committee and endorsed by Board. The Sitting fee of Independent Directors is also decided on the basis of Guidelines issued by DPE and the extant provisions of the Companies Act, 2013. Presently, the Company is paying ` 40,000/- per Member as sitting fees for Board Meetings and ` 30,000/- for Board level Committee Meetings.

# **Performance Evaluation** 

The Company is a Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE) and appointment/nomination of all the Directors including Independent Directors are being done by the President of India, through Administrative Ministry i.e. Mininstry of Petroleum & Natural Gas (MoP&NG) Government of India. Therefore, performance evaluation of Individual Directors is being undertaken by the Government of India, being the appointing authority. # **5. MEANS OF COMMUNICATION** 

The Company interacts/communicates with its stakeholders through Press Releases, AGM/EGM, Investors’ Meet, disclosures made to stock Exchanges and through Company’s website ‘www.oil-india.com’. Besides above, Company regularly sends letters and publishes Notices for payment of dividend, Record date, consideration of financial results, reminders for unclaimed dividends and shares, updation of PAN, Nomination details, KYC etc. 

## **a. Financial Results** 

The quarterly unaudited/audited financial results are announced within the time prescribed under the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015. The results are published in leading newspapers having wide circulation across the country and vernacular dailies having circulation in the state where the Registered Office of the Company is situated. The financial results are also hosted on the Company’s website. The Company issues news releases on significant corporate decisions / activities and posts them on its website as well as notifies the Stock Exchanges as and when deemed necessary. 

## **b. Conference call with Investors** 

The Company participates in conference calls to discuss the quarterly / annual financial performance of the Company and prior intimation thereof is given to the Stock Exchanges and is also hosted on the website of the Company. No unpublished price sensitive information is discussed in the meet/ presentation with institutional investors and financial analysts. 

191 



## **c. News Releases** 

Official press releases, detailed presentations made to Media/ Analysts/ Institutional Investors, etc. are displayed on the Company’s website. 

## **d. Website** 

The website of the Company (https://www.oil-india.com/) provides a separate section for Investors where all the information like Annual Reports, Shareholding Pattern, Notice of Board Meetings/ AGM, Window Closure Notices, Details of Dividends/ Shares transferred to IEPF Authority, formats for Investors, Corporate Governance Report etc. are available. The Company’s website also displays official news releases and other disclosures pursuant to RTI Act, 2005. 

## **e. Annual Report** 

The Annual Report containing inter alia Audited Financial Statements, Consolidated Audited Financial Statements, Boards’ Report, Auditors’ Report and other important information is circulated to members and others entitled thereto. The Company’s Annual Report is also available in downloadable form on the Company’s website. 

## **f. AGM/EGM** 

The General Meetings of the Company are being organized as per extant provisions, for which adequate advance notice is given to all shareholders of the Company. 

## **g. SCORES (SEBI Complaints Redressal System)** 

SEBI processes investors’ complaints in a centralized web-based complaints redressal system i.e. SCORES. Through this system, a shareholder can lodge complaint(s) against a Company for his grievance, Company/RTA uploads the action taken on the complaint which can be viewed by shareholders. 

## **h. Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) Portal** 

SEBI has established a common Online Dispute Resolution Portal (“ODR Portal”) for resolution of disputes arising in the Indian Securities. After exhausting the option to resolve their grievances with the RTA/ Company directly and through existing SCORES platform, the investors can initiate dispute resolution through the ODR Portal i.e. https:// smartodr.in/login 

## **i. Others** 

All periodical compliance filings like Shareholding Pattern, Integrated Filing (Governance), Media Releases, Integrated Filing (Finance), amongst others are filed electronically on NSE & BSE platform within the stipulated timelines. Further, the Company addressed various investor-centric letters/ emails to its shareholders during the year. These includes reminders for claiming unclaimed/ unpaid dividends from the Company, Dematerialization of shares, Updation of KYC email ids, Bank details etc. 

The Company has designated email ids viz investors@oilindia.in & investorrelation@oilindia.in for Retail Investors & Institutional Investors respectively and for responding to their queries.

# **6.6 Share Transfer System** 

The Shares of the Company are traded electronically in dematerialized form. Beneficiary gives purchase / sale instructions to their Depository Participants. Settlements of trades are done  on NSE / BSE which is connected to NSDL and CDSL. Confirmation in respect of the request for dematerialization of shares is sent to the respective depositories i.e. NSDL and CDSL expeditiously. 

Pursuant to SEBI circular dated 25.01.2022, the Company has been issuing securities in dematerialised form only while processing the requests for issue of duplicate share certificates, transmission, transposition etc., since no physical transfer of shares is allowed. Shareholders, who are still holding shares in physical form, are requested to get their shares dematerialized with depositories and get their credentials (KYC) updated with RTA before initiating action for dematerialization of securities. 

Certificate for timely dematerialization of the shares as per SEBI (Depositories and Participants) Regulations, 2018 are submitted to the Stock Exchange as per statutory timelines. In addition, as  a part of the capital integrity audit, a “Report on Reconciliation of Share Capital” confirming that the total issued capital of the Company is in agreement with the total listed capital, number of shares in physical form and the total number of dematerialized shares held with NSDL and CDSL, is submitted to the Stock Exchange and also placed before the Board at regular intervals. 

Pursuant to SEBI circular dated 02.07.2025 & 30.01.2026, a special window for transfer and dematerialization of physical securities has been extended till 04.02.2027 for shares sold/purchase prior to 01<sup>st</sup> April 2019 & re-lodgment of transfer deeds, which were submitted earlier and were rejected/returned/not attended to, due to deficiency in the documents/process/or otherwise. The documents completed in all aspects must be lodged with the Company/ RTA and the securities that are lodged for transfer shall be issued only in demat mode subject to compliance with due process for such transfer-cum-demat requests.

# **6.10  Commodity Price Risks / Foreign Exchange Risk and Hedging Activities** 

The Company is subject to commodity price risks due to fluctuation in prices of crude oil. The Company has in place a robust risk management framework for identification, monitoring and mitigation of commodity price and foreign exchange risks. The risks are tracked and monitored on a regular basis and mitigation strategies are adopted in line with the risk management framework. 

195 



# **6.11 Risk Management** 

The Company has institutionalized the Enterprise-wide Risk Management Program and Framework to not only provide a comprehensive view of our risk exposures but also to facilitate a risk informed decision-making, in this highly volatile business environment. The Board of Directors and the top management are cognizant of the need to equip the organization with the necessary framework and processes to effectively manage risks and navigate the complex risk environment in which it operates. We are consistently mapping the various levels of risks inherent in our business strategies and operations. 

A robust risk governance structure has been developed to enable greater oversight over the risk management process. Company follows a three-tier system of managing risks across the organization. 

- In the first level, the Operational Risk Management Committees (ORMC) review the status of implementation of Mitigation Plans carried out by respective Risk controllers, Risk owners and Risk Coordinators at Sphere level. 

- In the second level, the Risk Management Steering Committee (RMSC) reviews the status of Risk Assessment Parameters vis-à-vis identified Risk Tolerance level of individual risks at corporate level. 

- In the third and final stage, the Risk Management Committee (RMC) at Board level evaluates the Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) Framework of the Company and provides necessary guidance accordingly. 

Board of the Company has the ultimate responsibility towards the stakeholders of the Company, to ensure that there is adequate governance and oversight over the risks that can impact the business. In this regard, Risk Management Committee (RMC) who is responsible for assisting the Board abreast, has been reviewing the risk register and the mitigation actions periodically as per the guidelines laid down in the Risk Management Policy and framework adopted for the purpose. The Company, in its 572<sup>nd</sup> Board Meeting held on 09.10.2025 approved the revised Risk Management Policy, 2025 and Updated Risk Register ensuring organizational resilience, informed decision-making, regulatory compliance and sustainable performance

# **6.15 Disclosure in relation to Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace** 

The Company is committed towards prevention of sexual harassment of women at workplace and takes prompt action in the event of reporting of any such incidents. The Company has in place mechanism for prevention of sexual harassment in line with the requirements of the Sexual Harassment of Women at the Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013. In this regard, Internal Complaints Committees (ICCs) have been constituted at various offices of the Company to deal with sexual harassment complaints, if any and to conduct enquiries.

# **6.16 Awareness Sessions/ Workshops on Governance practices** 

Employees across the Company are regularly sensitized to the Company’s policies, governance framework and ethical practices. To strength the governance framework and promote ethical practice, the Company conducts in-house training workshops on Corporate Governance. These programmes cover the fundamentals of Corporate Governance as well as key internal policies and statutory requirements, including but not limited to the Code of Conduct, Whistle Blower Policy, SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 etc. 

# **6.17   Insider Trading** 

The Company has in place the Code of Conduct to Regulate, Monitor and Report Trading by Insiders” (The Code) and “Code of Practice and Procedures for Fair Disclosures in line with SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015. The Policy includes policy and procedure for inquiry in case of leak of UPSI or suspected leak of UPSI. 

For ensuring proper implementation of the SEBI Regulations, a Structured Digital Database of the designated employees is in place, for the purpose of monitoring their trades. A Digital Mechanism for maintaining confidentiality of the UPSI and ensuring compliance to the Code is also in place. 

The Weblink for the Code and Policy of the Company:

## **7.4 Details of Vigil Mechanism / Whistle Blower Policy** 

The Company endeavors to work against corruption in all its forms through well-defined Whistle Blower Policy. The policy provides all the employees with free access to the Management in case they observe unethical or improper practices or any other wrongful conduct in the Company and to prohibit managerial personnel from taking any adverse personal action against those employees. Further, no personnel have been denied access to the Audit & Ethics Committee of the Board. No complaint under the Vigil Mechanism was received during the year. 

Weblink of Policy: <u>https://www.oil-india.com/fles/investor_services_documents/Whistle_Blower_Policy.pdf</u> 

## **7.5 Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption Policy (ABAC)** 

The Company has adopted Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption (ABAC) Policy which serves as a guiding framework for ensuring compliance with applicable anti bribery and anti corruption laws, regulations and prescribed standards of ethical conduct. The Policy sets out the expected standards of behaviour and integrity to be adhered to by the Company and all its officials in the conduct of business. 

ABAC Policy is applicable to all employees of the Company working at all levels and is widely disseminated throughout the organisation. The Policy is available on the Company’s website at 

Weblink: <u>https://www.oil-india.com/fles/2026-08/Anti_Bribery_Anti_Corruption_Policy.pdf</u>
